def:finite-interface.title: Finite classical Einstein--Standard-Model interface
def:finite-interface.note: Encoded (FiniteInterfaceRepresentationTable.lean extends the (I1)-(I5) record FiniteInterface of FiniteEinsteinStandardModelInterface.lean). TabulatedFiniteInterface h adds the declared branch (minimal | neutrino), a linear equivalence tableEquiv : OneGeneration ~= C^{TableRow b} that INTERTWINES fermionRep with tableRep b, the block-diagonal sum of the table rows repQL, repLL (left) and repUR, repDR, repER (right), plus repNR on the neutrino branch, all taken from SMDescentYukawaBlocksExact.lean, and chirality with tableChirality b = diag(+1 on Q_L, L_L; -1 on u_R, d_R, e_R(, nu_R)) read off the chirality column of tab:SM-representations; the declared neutral blocks are identified with the neutral rows of the branch (neutralEquiv). Derived consequences: fermionRep and chirality are determined by the table (fermionRep_eq_table, chirality_eq_table), one generation has dimension 15 / 16 (finrank_oneGeneration_minimal / _neutrino), and v is left-handed iff its right-row components vanish (chirality_eq_self_iff). Constructor from data: ofTable builds the record from the (I1), (I3)-(I5) data and the branch, producing the fermion carrier, representation, chirality and the involution/equivariance fields from the table (tableChirality_mul_self, tableChirality_commute). Non-vacuity: trivialGeometryInterface (one site, flat coframe, Gram = id), whose G_SM action is nontrivial (example in the file: the cover element (1, 1, e^{i pi/6}) acts by -1 on e_R). Still disclosed (accepted as minor by the audit): relabeling covariance and the smooth comparison cylinder / reconstruction map of (I1) are not encoded; the Majorana charge-conjugate doubling concerns the bilinear, not the representation rows. Checklist (b): the fermion representation is tied to the table and constructed from it.

def:tests.title: Physical variation space
def:tests.note: Rendering (disclosed, common to the six records): M = (0,T) x T^3 (the paper allows any closed 3-manifold Sigma; its quantitative theorems live on T^3); fields and tests are represented by their spatially Z^3-periodic lifts to R^4 = Fin 4 -> R (cylProj_add_spatialShift: they descend to R x UnitAddTorus (Fin 3)); bundles trivialised ('after fixed local gauge and spin-frame identifications'); flat comparison metric and Lebesgue density; fibres: coframe / metric test Fin 4 -> Fin 4 -> R; ad P = smLie = s(u(3)+u(2)) in the defining 5x5 block representation of G_SM = S(U(3)xU(2)) (skew-Hermitian, block-diagonal, trace 0); Higgs C^2 with rho_H = the u(2) block (Lie-algebra form of the library's higgsRep); spinors C^4 (Weyl basis) tensor a finite fermion-carrier index type C, the chiral bundle cut out by IsChiral / IsCoChiral (left rows carry only the gamma5 = +1 components, right rows only gamma5 = -1; dual spinor opposite); fibre norms are Pi sup norms (equivalent to the fixed bundle metrics). testSubmodule left K is V_K: tuples v = (k, a, eta_H, eta_Psi, eta_Psibar) of C^infty, spatially periodic sections with tsupport inside cylProj^-1 K (K : CylRegion T, a compact subset of (0,T) x T^3), k symmetric (k^{mu nu} = delta g^{mu nu}), a smLie-valued (ad P one-form), spinor entries chiral. The C^r test norm is testNorm r = sum over the five entries of crNorm r f = sum_{j<=r} sup_x ||D^j f(x)|| (Mathlib iteratedFDeriv, operator norm of the j-th derivative; equivalent to the multi-index sup norms of the flat atlas). IsCylTest.bddAbove_norm_iteratedFDeriv proves the suprema are finite (periodicity + time support in (0,T) + a compact fundamental box); CrTest.normedSpaceCore proves the C^r test norm is a norm (definiteness from the j = 0 term), giving NormedAddCommGroup / NormedSpace R instances on CrTest left r K (a type synonym of V_K). The completion V_K^r = CrTestCompletion left r K is the abstract completion UniformSpace.Completion (a real Banach space), for every integer r; r_0 >= 4 is the field RegulatorSequence.r0 (four_le_r0). 'Determining core' = IsDeterminingCore (a subspace of V_K dense in V_K^r; isDeterminingCore_top: V_K itself); the clause 'with the stated uniform bounds extending to its completion' refers to bounds stated elsewhere (extension by continuity) and is not separately encoded. Non-vacuity: bumpTest (k = phi(t) delta, phi a smooth time bump supported in [T/4,3T/4], K = [T/4,3T/4] x T^3) is a nonzero test (norm_bumpTest_pos).

def:regulator.title: A finite-interface regulator sequence
def:regulator.note: Rendering (disclosed, common to the six records): M = (0,T) x T^3 (the paper allows any closed 3-manifold Sigma; its quantitative theorems live on T^3); fields and tests are represented by their spatially Z^3-periodic lifts to R^4 = Fin 4 -> R (cylProj_add_spatialShift: they descend to R x UnitAddTorus (Fin 3)); bundles trivialised ('after fixed local gauge and spin-frame identifications'); flat comparison metric and Lebesgue density; fibres: coframe / metric test Fin 4 -> Fin 4 -> R; ad P = smLie = s(u(3)+u(2)) in the defining 5x5 block representation of G_SM = S(U(3)xU(2)) (skew-Hermitian, block-diagonal, trace 0); Higgs C^2 with rho_H = the u(2) block (Lie-algebra form of the library's higgsRep); spinors C^4 (Weyl basis) tensor a finite fermion-carrier index type C, the chiral bundle cut out by IsChiral / IsCoChiral (left rows carry only the gamma5 = +1 components, right rows only gamma5 = -1; dual spinor opposite); fibre norms are Pi sup norms (equivalent to the fixed bundle metrics). RegulatorSequence T FC bundles: r0 >= 4; cofinal cutoffs h_n > 0, h_n -> 0 (the cofinal family is rendered as a sequence); interfaces iface n : TabulatedFiniteInterface h_n (the ledger encoding of def:finite-interface) with a fixed identification of their Yukawa sectors (bank n = theta_h carried by the interface); configurations z_h^d = config n; reconstruction maps recon n : Config -> SmoothFields (C^infty on the open slab, spatially periodic, A smLie-valued, chiral spinors); linear test lifts lift n K : V_K ->_R Config (= T_{z^d} Q_h) supported in a fixed enlargement K' = enlarge K with K inside int K'. Support of a finite configuration is given meaning by added site-locality data (sitePos : Site -> M and projections siteComp onto site degrees of freedom: complete, idempotent, orthogonal, compatible with the local coframe / Higgs readers), because the library's def:finite-interface encoding has no site decomposition of Q_h (disclosed addition). c_h(K) = consistencyDefect n K = sum_{b in {g,SM}} sup_{v in V_K, ||v||_{C^r0} <= 1} |D S_{b,h}(z^d)[I_h v] - D S_{b,theta_h}(z_h)[v]| and eps_h(K) = stationarityDefect n K = sup |D S_h(z^d)[I_h v]|: literal suprema over V_K valued in [0,infty] (no boundedness presupposed); FirstVariationConsistent / PhysicallyStationary = these tend to 0 for every K. S_{g,h} = gravityAction and S_{SM,h} = nu * matterAction of the library interface (so S_h = S_{g,h} + S_{SM,h}: fderiv_action_eq_sum); sectorwise differentiability at z^d is a field. The continuum variation D S_{b,theta}(z)[v] = firstVariation = d/de at 0 of the integral over the fundamental domain (0,T) x [0,1)^3 of (L_b(z + e vhat) - L_b(z)), vhat = (edot(k), a, eta_H, eta_Psi, eta_Psibar), edot = metricLift (eq:metric-lift; spinor components held fixed, spin-connection variation kept). The densities are written out literally: gravity (Scal(g) - 2 Lambda)/(2 kappa) sqrt|det g| via Gravity/CoordinateCurvature (the paper's curvature conventions); Yang-Mills -1/4 g g <F,F> with F = dA + A wedge A; Higgs -g^{mu nu} Re<DH, DH> - lambda(|H|^2 - v^2)^2; Dirac-Yukawa Re{(i/2)[Psibar gamma^mu nabla Psi - (nabla Psibar) gamma^mu Psi] - Psibar M_Y(H) Psi} with Weyl-basis Clifford matrices (gammaW_clifford: gamma^a gamma^b + gamma^b gamma^a = 2 eta^{ab}), the Levi-Civita spin connection of e and gamma^mu = E^mu_a gamma^a; all times sqrt|det g|. Doubts / renderings: (i) the smooth Einstein-Hilbert density is used (reconstructions are smooth and tests compactly supported, so it agrees with the app:palatini first-derivative representative; the low-regularity Palatini definition is not encoded here); (ii) the base normalisations of the invariant Lie-algebra metric (-2 tr on su(3), su(2); hypercharge Y = diag(-1/3,-1/3,-1/3,1/2,1/2)) are standard choices - the paper only names the coefficients g_j^{-2}; (iii) the internal fermion data enter through FermionCarrier (finite carrier, chirality labels, R-linear skew-Hermitian bracket- and chirality-preserving rho_F, real-affine Yukawa map with constant Majorana part allowed, infinitesimally gauge covariant) - exactly the properties the paper says the analysis uses - and are not derived from the interface's tabulated group representation. Non-vacuity: trivialRegulator (flat constant fields over trivialGeometryInterface, zero lifts), physically stationary (trivialRegulator_stationary).

prop:source-bound.title: Scaled source control of physical stationarity
prop:source-bound.note: Proved. The positive source space with Gram G_h is a real inner-product space W (its norm is the G_h norm); the finite action covector a_h is a continuous linear functional a : W ->L[R] R whose operator norm is the dual norm ||a_h||_{G_h^{-1}} (source_bound), equivalently the G_h-norm of its Riesz representative alpha (source_bound_riesz, using innerSL_apply_norm). The test space V is any real normed space (the C^{r_0} norm), v_h : V -> W the source lift, and Phi v = D S_h(z_h^d)[I_h v]. stationarityDefect Phi := iSup over the unit ball of |Phi v| encodes eps_h(K) of eq:stationarity. From ||a||^2 <= R_h, ||v_h(v)|| <= L_h ||v|| and |Phi v - a(v_h v)| <= e_h ||v||, source_bound_pointwise gives |Phi v| <= (L_h sqrt R_h + e_h)||v|| (Cauchy-Schwarz = ContinuousLinearMap.le_opNorm, sqrt monotonicity, triangle inequality) and source_bound gives eps_h(K) <= L_h sqrt R_h + e_h (ciSup_le over the nonempty unit ball). The 'in particular' clause is source_bound_tendsto: along a regulator sequence, L_h sqrt R_h + e_h -> 0 forces eps_h(K) -> 0 (squeeze_zero with stationarityDefect_nonneg_of_bound). Scoped hypotheses disclosed: the constants L_h, e_h are taken nonnegative (needed only to pass from the ||v||-scaled bound to the unit-ball supremum); the lift v_h need not be linear; the earlier pointer gt_protected_riesz was not needed.

def:reduced-topology.title: Reduced action convergence
def:reduced-topology.note: Rendering (disclosed, common to the six records): M = (0,T) x T^3 (the paper allows any closed 3-manifold Sigma; its quantitative theorems live on T^3); fields and tests are represented by their spatially Z^3-periodic lifts to R^4 = Fin 4 -> R (cylProj_add_spatialShift: they descend to R x UnitAddTorus (Fin 3)); bundles trivialised ('after fixed local gauge and spin-frame identifications'); flat comparison metric and Lebesgue density; fibres: coframe / metric test Fin 4 -> Fin 4 -> R; ad P = smLie = s(u(3)+u(2)) in the defining 5x5 block representation of G_SM = S(U(3)xU(2)) (skew-Hermitian, block-diagonal, trace 0); Higgs C^2 with rho_H = the u(2) block (Lie-algebra form of the library's higgsRep); spinors C^4 (Weyl basis) tensor a finite fermion-carrier index type C, the chiral bundle cut out by IsChiral / IsCoChiral (left rows carry only the gamma5 = +1 components, right rows only gamma5 = -1; dual spinor opposite); fibre norms are Pi sup norms (equivalent to the fixed bundle metrics). ReducedConvergence Q z theta L theta0 (one compact chart) and RegulatorSequence.ReducedActionConvergence (every chart, reconstructed fields R_h(z_h^d)): the clauses of eq:reduced-topology - e_h -> e strongly in H^1 (H1Tendsto; the limit in H^1 with weak gradient de: MemH1 = every component in SobolevOpen.MemW12); e_h(x), e(x) in K_e a.e., K_e a fixed compact subset of coframeChart = {det e > 0, e^0_0 > 0} (oriented, time-oriented, nondegenerate: the convention of the library's def:finite-interface encoding); A_h -> A in L^4; F_{A_h} -> F_A in L^2 with F_A identified weakly with A (HasWeakCurvature: F - [A,A] = dA in D'(Q)); H_h -> H in L^2; D_{A_h}H_h -> D_A H in L^2 (HasWeakCovGrad: K - rho_H(A)H = dH in D'(Q)); Psi_h, Psibar_h converge weakly in H^1; the banks lie in a compact subset of {kappa, g_j, lambda_H > 0} (bankCoords into (Fin 7 -> R) x (Ysec -> M_3(C))) and converge; the limit A is smLie-valued a.e. Renderings: a compact smooth chart K is a closed coordinate box (ChartBox: 0 < a_0 < b_0 < T, spatial sides <= 1 so it injects into T^3; L^p(K) = L^p(box), H^1(K) = W^{1,2}(box), as in the ledger encoding of prop:orlicz); weak H^1 convergence (WeakH1Tendsto) = all terms and the limit in W^{1,2}(Q), a uniform W^{1,2}(Q) bound and convergence of all C_c^infty(Q) test pairings of components and gradients (equivalent to weak convergence in the Hilbert space H^1(Q): stated, not proved in Lean); multi-component L^p norms with the sup fibre norm. The two explanatory sentences after the display (strong H^1 cap L^4 Higgs convergence follows from prop:covariant-higgs-endpoint; no L^infty coframe convergence is asserted) are remarks, not clauses. Non-vacuity: flatRegulator_reducedActionConvergence (the flat regulator with a physical bank converges to flatLimit on every chart).

def:reduced-certificate.title: Reduced compactness certificate
def:reduced-certificate.note: Rendering (disclosed, common to the six records): M = (0,T) x T^3 (the paper allows any closed 3-manifold Sigma; its quantitative theorems live on T^3); fields and tests are represented by their spatially Z^3-periodic lifts to R^4 = Fin 4 -> R (cylProj_add_spatialShift: they descend to R x UnitAddTorus (Fin 3)); bundles trivialised ('after fixed local gauge and spin-frame identifications'); flat comparison metric and Lebesgue density; fibres: coframe / metric test Fin 4 -> Fin 4 -> R; ad P = smLie = s(u(3)+u(2)) in the defining 5x5 block representation of G_SM = S(U(3)xU(2)) (skew-Hermitian, block-diagonal, trace 0); Higgs C^2 with rho_H = the u(2) block (Lie-algebra form of the library's higgsRep); spinors C^4 (Weyl basis) tensor a finite fermion-carrier index type C, the chiral bundle cut out by IsChiral / IsCoChiral (left rows carry only the gamma5 = +1 components, right rows only gamma5 = -1; dual spinor opposite); fibre norms are Pi sup norms (equivalent to the fixed bundle metrics). ReducedCertificate Q z theta, one field per item: (R1) coframe values a.e. in one fixed compact subset of coframeChart, an H^1(Q) bound, a common compact L^2 screen for the first-derivative packet d_i e^a_mu; (R2) connections precompact in L^4 (LpPrecompact: every term in L^p and finite eps-nets drawn from the sequence, i.e. total boundedness), curvature packet F_{A_h} bounded in L^2 with a common compact screen; (R3) Higgs bounded in L^2, covariant-gradient packet bounded with a common compact screen; (R4) Psi_h, Psibar_h bounded in H^1 (no spinor screen); (R5) banks in a compact subset of the physical region. RegulatorSequence.SatisfiesReducedCertificate applies it to the reconstructed fields. 'Common compact screen' is encoded literally as the hypotheses of lem:screen (the paper's definition): CommonCompactScreen Y = there are bounded S_{h,R} and compact S_R (Mathlib IsCompactOperator, R in N) with ||S_{h,R} - S_R|| -> 0 for each R, lim_R sup_h ||(I - S_{h,R}) Y_h|| = 0 (eps form), and S_R Y -> Y for every weak subsequential limit Y of (Y_h) (the weak-limit clause of lem:screen imposed on every weak cluster point because the certificate is stated before extraction - disclosed reading); HasCommonCompactScreen transports a packet into the Hilbert space L^2(Q; EuclideanSpace C iota). Non-vacuity: flatRegulator_reducedCertificate (every chart).

thm:reduced-closure.title: Reduced Einstein--Standard-Model variational closure
thm:reduced-closure.note: Proved. reduced_closure: for a regulator sequence reg (def:regulator) satisfying the reduced compactness certificate (R1)-(R5) on every chart box, first-variation consistency c_h(K)->0 and physical stationarity eps_h(K)->0 for every K (FirstVariationConsistent, PhysicallyStationary; the manuscript's hypothesis L_h sqrt(R_h)+e_h->0 implies eps_h(K)->0 by prop:source-bound, so this is a weakening of the hypothesis), every cutoff subsequence ns has a further subsequence ns o psi, limit fields L and a limiting bank theta0 with: theta0 physical; on every slab chart ReducedConvergence (strong H^1 coframes with terms and limit a.e. in one compact subset of the oriented time-oriented nondegenerate coframe chart, no uniform convergence; A_h->A in L^4 with smLie-valued limit; F_{A_h}->F in L^2 with F=dA+A^A weakly (identity passed to the limit, hasWeakCurvature_of_tendsto); H_h->H, D_{A_h}H_h->D_AH in L^2 with D_AH identified weakly; weak H^1 spinors; bank convergence in the compact physical set) and HiggsH1L4Convergence (H_h->H strongly in H^1 cap L^4 with gradient D_AH - rho_H(A)H, prop:covariant-higgs-endpoint); the complete reconstructed first variation (gravity + Yang-Mills + Higgs + full Dirac-Yukawa) converges in (V_K^{r0})^* (actionVariation_dual_tendsto); the limit is a distributional solution of all Euler equations: gravLimitVariation + smLimitVariation = 0 on every test of every V_K (residual bound eq:reduced-residual-bound: limit_eq_zero_of_defects + homogeneity); eq:reduced-Einstein-limit: einsteinDistribution = kappa * stressDistribution on metric tests, with <(Ein(g)+Lambda g)dV_g,k> := 2 kappa D S_g[k] (first-order/integrated-by-parts representative of app:palatini, gravLimitVariation) and <T^SM dV_g,k> := -2 D_g S_SM[k] (eq:stress-definition, smLimitVariation incl. the spin-connection chain), both evaluated on the metric part (k,0,0,0,0) of the test. Compactness: Rellich (w12_compactness_box) + lem:screen (screen_strong_convergence, with the new links: weak sequential compactness in L^2 and complete continuity of compact operators) for the coframe, curvature and covariant-gradient packets; L^4 precompactness of A; prop:covariant-higgs-endpoint (covariant_higgs_endpoint_box); weak H^1 compactness for spinors; compact bank set; diagonal argument over the slab exhaustion (T/(m+3), T-T/(m+3))x(0,1)^3 with one patched limit (uniqueness of reduced limits a.e. + a.e. invariance). Scoped hypothesis (disclosed): FermionCarrier.YukawaContinuous (the carrier encoding leaves the bank -> Yukawa map abstract; in the manuscript it is a fixed linear function of the bank's Yukawa matrices). Renderings (accepted, disclosed again): M=(0,T)xT^3 lifted to R^4 with spatially Z^3-periodic fields, trivialised bundles, compact charts rendered as chart boxes, H^1(Q)=W^{1,2}(Q) with weak gradients as data, dual norms of V_K^r rendered as the uniform estimate |l_h(v)-l(v)| <= eps ||v||_{C^r} eventually; the conclusions are stated on every slab chart box (t0,t1)x(0,1)^3, 0<t0<t1<T (a fundamental domain of the spatial torus; ReducedConvergence.mono gives every chart box inside a slab; boxes straddling a spatial period differ by a Z^3 translation of periodic fields, not formalised). Non-vacuity: the flat regulator satisfies every hypothesis (flatRegulator_consistent: its continuum first variations vanish, firstVariation_flat; flatRegulator_stationary; example after them). Standard axioms only.

prop:covariant-higgs-endpoint.title: Covariant-gradient compactness closes the Higgs endpoint
prop:covariant-higgs-endpoint.note: Proved on a coordinate box Q = prod_i (a_i, b_i) in a four-dimensional chart (disclosed rendering of the bounded smooth chart K, as for prop:orlicz). Renderings: the Higgs field has m complex components H_h^c, each in H^1(Q) = W^{1,2}(Q) with weak gradient dH_h (the manuscript's smooth reconstructed fields are in particular in H^1(Q); only H^1 is assumed); the connection enters through the matrix entries A_h mu c e = rho_H(A_{h,mu})_{ce} (A_h -> A in L^4 gives entrywise L^4 convergence since rho_H is linear); D_A H = dH + A H (covD). covariant_higgs_endpoint_box: from A_h -> A_0 in L^4(Q), sup_h ||H_h||_{L^2(Q)} < infinity and D_{A_h} H_h -> Y in L^2(Q), a subsequence converges to some H_0 with H_0 in H^1(Q), weak gradient covGrad = Y - A_0 H_0 (i.e. Y = D_{A_0} H_0, covD_covGrad), strongly in H^1(Q) (values and weak gradients in L^2(Q)) and strongly in L^4(Q); covariant_higgs_endpoint_box_precompact: the same for every subsequence (precompactness in H^1(Q)); covariant_higgs_endpoint_box_of_L2: if H_h -> H_0 in L^2(Q) is known (any subsequential L^2 limit), Y = D_{A_0} H_0 and the whole sequence converges in H^1(Q) and L^4(Q); higgs_densities_tendsto: conj(H^c) H^e converge in L^2, the quartic products and conj(D^c_mu) D^e_nu in L^1 (the quartic potential lambda(|H|^2 - v^2)^2 and the Higgs stress are fixed linear combinations of these with constant reference-chart coefficients; for convergent bounded coefficients LpProductContinuity.LpTendsto.coeff applies). Proof as in the manuscript: relative multiplier estimate ||alpha w||_2 <= eps ||w||_4 + C_eps ||w||_2 for fixed alpha in L^4 (truncation, exists_relative_multiplier), critical Sobolev H^1(Q) -> L^4(Q) (eLpNorm_le_box: Mathlib's Gagliardo-Nirenberg-Sobolev inequality for C^1_c functions extended to W^{1,2}_c by mollification, eLpNorm_le_sum_grad_of_ball, plus the box extension), absorption giving an eventual uniform H^1 bound (covariant_eventually_bounded), Rellich on the box (rellich_box_family), compact multiplication (tendsto_eLpNorm_mul_of_L4) for A_h H_h -> A_0 H_0 in L^2, passage of weak derivatives to L^2 limits (hasWeakPartial_of_tendsto), and Sobolev on the differences for L^4. lem:products is not used as a hypothesis (the needed Hoelder products are proved here or taken from Analysis/MollifierLpConvergence LpTendsto.bilin). Non-vacuity: example after higgs_densities_tendsto (constant field, zero connection, unit box of R^4). Standard axioms only.

prop:weak-fermion.title: Weak-$H^1$ continuity of the complete fermionic first variation
prop:weak-fermion.note: Proved in the slab-box rendering. diracVariation_dual_tendsto: on the slab chart box Q=(t0,t1)x(0,1)^3 containing the time support of K, if the coframes take values a.e. in one compact subset of the coframe chart and converge strongly in H^1(Q), A_h->A and H_h->H strongly in L^2(Q), Psi_h, Psibar_h converge weakly in H^1(Q) (WeakH1Tendsto) and the Yukawa coefficients converge (linear part in operator norm and constant), then the complete first variation of the Dirac-Yukawa action actionVariation T (diracDensity*volFactor) along variationDirection (metric lift incl. the spin-connection chain omega=P(e)de, gauge, Higgs, spinor variations) converges in the dual norm of V_K^r for every r>=1 (paper: r>=2), rendered as: for all eps>0, eventually |DS_h(v)-DS(v)|<=eps*||v||_{C^r} for all tests. The L^2 hypotheses cover the paper's L^4 form (diracVariation_dual_tendsto_L4) and its weakening (strong L^2 + uniform L^4); no strong convergence of spinor derivatives and no uniform coframe convergence is used. Ingredients: factorization diracDensity*vol = diracPt(redJet) (spinConn_eq_spinConnL), covector split strong/weak, Rellich (tendsto_L2_box_of_weak), Sobolev L^4 (exists_sobolev_L4_box), critical (2,4,4) trilinear products, finite-net weak-strong pairing on the C^1 unit ball (uniform_weak_strong_op). Renderings disclosed: hypotheses on the slab box (a compact neighbourhood of K covering the spatial torus) rather than on K itself; the limit functional diracLimitVariation is the covector formula evaluated on the limit jet (low-regularity D S_D); Yukawa convergence assumed because FermionCarrier.yukawa is an arbitrary function of the bank; the 'no independent fermionic Hilbert-stress defect' sentence is the interpretation of the metric-direction part of the same convergence.

prop:reduced-continuity.title: Continuity in the reduced action topology
prop:reduced-continuity.note: Proved in the slab-box rendering, all four sectors. actionVariation_dual_tendsto: under ReducedConvergence (def:reduced-topology) on the slab chart box Q=(t0,t1)x(0,1)^3 whose open time interval contains the time support of K (CylRegion.exists_slab_Ioo), and convergence of the carrier's Yukawa map, for every r>=1 (paper r>=2) D S_{theta_h}(z_h) = firstVariation .gravity + firstVariation .standardModel converges to the limit first variation in the dual norm of V_K^r, rendered as: for all eps>0, eventually |DS_h(v)-DS(v)| <= eps*||v||_{C^r} for all tests. Separately per sector: gravity gravVariation_dual_tendsto; Yang-Mills+Higgs bosonVariation_dual_tendsto (incl. metric rows, L^4 Higgs via prop:covariant-higgs-endpoint = higgs_L4_tendsto); complete Dirac-Yukawa incl. metric-spin-connection chain diracVariation_dual_tendsto; SM total smVariation_dual_tendsto. Gravity: firstVariation .gravity uses the library's second-order density (scalarCurvF with dChristoffelF); scalarCurv_vol_eq proves sqrt|g| R = L1(e,de) + sum_c d_c W^c pointwise for smooth coframes, integral_div_slab_eq_zero kills the divergence (divergence theorem on boxes: time faces vanish, spatial faces cancel by periodicity), so gravVariation_eq_firstOrder identifies D S_g with the first variation of the first-order representative (L1 - 2 Lambda vol)/(2 kappa), L1 = Q(e)(de,de) (metric Gamma-Gamma form; the manuscript calls it Palatini-type), whose covector converges in L^1 (gravCov_tendsto) under H^1-strong coframes in a compact chart. Renderings disclosed: slab box instead of an arbitrary chart around K; limit functionals (gravLimitVariation, smLimitVariation) are the first-order covector formulas evaluated on the limit jet (the low-regularity D S of the limit fields); the Yukawa convergence hypothesis (yukL and the constant term) is needed only because FermionCarrier.yukawa is an arbitrary function of the bank (in the paper the Yukawa matrices are bank coordinates); the 'Hilbert stress, not an independent tensor' sentence is the metric-direction part of the same limit functional. Non-vacuity: flat regulator example.

cor:reduced-stress.title: Reconstructed and operational stress in the reduced class

(v) eq:bounded-chart-composition: chart_composition (compact chart rendered as a coordinate box Q, as for prop:orlicz; H^1(Q) = W^{1,2}(Q) with weak gradients as data): if e_h, e in H^1(Q) take values a.e. in a compact set K_e and e_h -> e strongly in H^1(Q), then for every Phi that is C^1 on an open U containing K_e (flattened coordinates) -- in particular every smooth F(e,e^{-1}) on a compact subset of the nondegenerate chart (contDiffOn_coeff_frame) -- Phi(e_h), Phi(e) are in H^1(Q) with weak gradients DPhi(e) d e (the weak chain rule, new generic theorem SobolevOpen.MemW12.comp_of_mem_compact, proved by cutoff + mollification + dominated convergence; the gradient appears with Re of the complex gradient data of the real coframe components), Phi(e_h) -> Phi(e) strongly in H^1(Q), sup_h ||Phi(e_h)||_oo < oo, and Phi(e_h) -> Phi(e) in every finite L^p(Q). (vi) eq:spin-connection-convergence: the library Levi-Civita spin connection spinConn (used by firstVariation) equals P(e) d e, spinConn_eq_spinConnL, with P = spinConnL e a continuous linear map of the jet, smooth on GL = {det e != 0} (contDiffOn_spinConnL; d E = -E de E is pd_frameAt, d g is pd_metricAt); omega(e_h) -> omega(e) in L^2(Q): spinConn_L2_tendsto_of_h1; the metric variation: for the symmetric lift ė(k) = -1/2 e g k (metricLiftL = metricLift, eq:metric-lift), d/deps omega(e + eps ė(k))(x) = spinConnVar(e,de)[k,dk] = (DP(e)[ė(k)]) de + P(e)(Dė(e)[de] k + ė(dk)) = P_1(e) k de + P_2(e) dk (hasDerivAt_spinConn_metricLift); the operators (k,dk) |-> spinConnVar(e_h, de_h)[k,dk] converge in L^2(Q) in operator norm (spinVarOp_L2_tendsto_of_h1), hence uniformly over every family of test fields with ||(k,dk)||_oo <= 1, in particular bounded C^1 test sets (spinConnVar_uniform). Only convergence in measure of e_h (from strong H^1) and values in the compact chart are used: no L^oo convergence. Rendering: compact chart = coordinate box (disclosed, as for prop:orlicz); coframe chart K_e a compact subset of GL (the paper's oriented time-oriented chart is a subset). Non-vacuity: example after contDiffOn_coeff_frame (flat coframe, coefficient (e^{-1})^0_0). Standard axioms only.

lem:screen.title: Common compact screen
lem:screen.note: screen_strong_convergence proves the first assertion on a complex Hilbert space for N-indexed sequences: bounded Z_n weakly convergent, ||S_{h,R} - S_R|| -> 0, uniform tail exhaustion, S_R Z -> Z, with compactness of S_R rendered as complete continuity (bounded weakly convergent inputs have strongly convergent images, equivalent for compact operators on Hilbert space) and the norm bound sup ||Z_n|| < infinity spelled out explicitly (automatic from weak convergence). The whitened clause is strong_convergence_transfer: uniformly bounded, strongly convergent B_n = A_h^{-1/2} applied to the strongly convergent whitened packet gives Y_h -> Y; the Loewner bounds mI <= A_h <= MI enter only through that uniform bound.

prop:time-compactness.title: From spatial screens to spacetime compactness
prop:time-compactness.note: Proved in greater generality. L^2(0,T;H) = Mathlib Bochner space Lp H 2 (volume.restrict (Ioc 0 T)); H any real normed space that is also a normed space over RCLike 𝕜 (H = L^2(Σ;E) is a special case; completeness only for the compact-closure/subsequence forms). P_R: any bounded idempotent 𝕜-linear operators with finite-dimensional range (orthogonality, smooth ranges and P_R -> I strongly are not needed). Tail hypothesis in the form 'for every ε there is R with sup_h ||(I-P_R)Y_h||_{L^2_t H} <= ε' (implied by the paper's lim_R sup_h = 0). H^1(0,T;P_R H) boundedness encoded by the absolutely continuous representative: P_R Y_h(t) = v0 + ∫_0^t g a.e. with ||g||_{L^2(0,T)} <= C_R uniformly in h (the L^2 part follows from sup_h ||Y_h||). Conclusion: TotallyBounded (range Y) (timeCompactness_totallyBounded), compact closure and convergent subsequences for complete H. Proof as in the paper: 1D Rellich via the Hölder-1/2 bound ||∫_a^b g|| <= sqrt(b-a)||g||_2 and uniform-partition step functions with values in the finite-dimensional range (a bounded subset of a finite-dimensional subspace of L^2_t H), then an ε-net from the tail. Final assertion ('follows from a bound on ∂_t Y_h in L^2(0,T;H^{-m})'): h1_bound_of_tested_derivative_bound, rendered abstractly since Σ, E, H^m are unspecified: P_R x = Σ_j φ_{R,j}(x) e_{R,j} (e.g. φ = <e_{R,j},·> for an orthonormal smooth basis of the range) and the tested derivatives satisfy φ_{R,j}(Y_h(t)) = a + ∫_0^t w with |w(s)| <= ν_{R,j} D_h(s), ν_{R,j} = V-norm (H^m-norm) of the test vector, D_h(s) = ||∂_t Y_h(s)||_{V^*}, sup_h ||D_h||_{L^2(0,T)} < ∞; conclusion is exactly the H^1 hypothesis. Non-vacuity example in the file (Y_i(t) = sin(i) t, P_R = I on ℝ).

prop:variation-continuity.title: First-variation continuity from primitive fields
prop:variation-continuity.note: PROVED (sector by sector, dual test norm): variation_continuity: for a slab chart Q=(t0,t1)x(0,1)^3, a test region K with time support in (t0,t1), test order r>=1, a compact coframe chart set Ke (IsCompactCoframeSet), a compact physical bank set P (IsCompactBankSet) and B<inf, there is C_K<inf such that for all smooth fields z1,z2 in the bounded strong-packet class PacketBound Q Ke B (coframe values in Ke on closure Q; ||e||_{H^1}, ||A||_{L^4}, ||F_A||_{L^2}, ||H||_{L^4}, ||D_A H||_{L^2}, ||Psi||_{H^1}, ||Psibar||_{H^1} <= B on Q), all theta1,theta2 in P, both sectors b in {g, SM} and all v in V_K: |DS_{b,theta1}(z1)[v] - DS_{b,theta2}(z2)[v]| <= C_K d_K(z1,theta1;z2,theta2) ||v||_{C^r} (ENNReal form), d_K = dK of EinsteinSMCofinalTransport (L^inf+H^1 coframe, L^4 connection, L^2 curvature, L^4 Higgs, L^2 covariant Higgs gradient, H^1 spinors, bank distance). Proof: covector identities gravVariation_eq_cov / smVariation_eq_cov; L^1(Q) Lipschitz estimates of the jet covectors, sector by sector: grav_lipschitz (3 coefficient terms gravC1/2/3 with bank scalars (2kappa)^-1, -(2kappa)^-1 2Lambda), boson_lipschitz (Yang-Mills pieces x gauge scalars g_j^-2, Higgs-kinetic pieces, Higgs potential (|H|^2-v^2)H and (|H|^2-v^2)^2 via constant-bilinear Hoelder (4,4)->2 and (2,2)->1, x lambda_H), dirac_lipschitz (strong bilinear strongCoeff1 (potential variable (de,A,M_Y(H),1;M_Y^lin) x spinor pair), strong trilinear strongCoeff2 (L^2 x L^4 x L^4), weak part as bilinear coefficient weakDirac in (1,Psibar,Psi) x spinor gradients); generic uniform lemmas coeff1_lip/coeff2_lip/coeff3_lip (C^1 coefficients bounded and Lipschitz on compact chart sets, Hoelder (inf,1), (inf,2,2), (inf,2,4,4)); jet distance of reduced jets <= 10(1+C_S) d_K (jetDist_redJet_le; spinor L^4 differences by the critical Sobolev embedding H^1(Q) -> L^4(Q), SobolevOpen.exists_sobolev_L4_box); bank bounds from compactness (exists_bankBounds: kappa,g_j >= c>0, all couplings <= M_b). Hypothesis beyond the manuscript (disclosed rendering of the abstract FermionCarrier, analogue of the YukawaContinuous hypothesis used throughout the ledger): YukawaLipOn FC P Ly My (M_Y^lin and M_Y(0) bounded and Lipschitz in the bank on P; automatic in the manuscript where M_Y is linear in the Yukawa matrices, which are bank coordinates; satisfied by the trivial carrier, yukawaLipOn_trivial). Renderings: bounded strong-packet class rendered by PacketBound with one common bound B (non-vacuous: exists_packetBound puts every smooth field with coframe values in Ke into the class for some finite B); dual norm of V_K^r rendered as |l1(v)-l2(v)| <= C ||v|| for all v; M=(0,T)xT^3 lifted to R^4 with Z^3-periodic fields, trivialised bundles (as in EinsteinSMReducedClosure). Non-vacuity: flat_packetBound and the example after it (trivial carrier, flat coframe set, physical bank, flat fields satisfy all hypotheses). Axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound only.

prop:weak-palatini.title: Weak-curvature Palatini passage
prop:weak-palatini.note: weak_palatini_passage_with_volume_variation proves every clause with formal content on a finite measure space (the compact region) with concrete L^p seminorms (eLpNorm/eLpNorm'): under eq:Palatini-hypotheses (e_h -> e in L^2, ||e_h||_6, ||e||_6 <= M, p > 3/2, R_h bounded in L^p with all pairings against L^{p'} tests converging): (1) B(e_h) -> B(e) in L^{p'}; (2) Palatini pairings converge; (3) volume densities vol(e_h^4) -> vol(e^4) in L^1; (4) for coframe variations k_h -> k in L^2 bounded in L^6, the Palatini first-variation pairings converge and (5) NEW: the volume (cosmological-term) variation densities vol(k_h,e_h,e_h,e_h) -> vol(k,e,e,e) in L^1 (eLpNorm_volume_variation_tendsto_zero, via the general four-factor passage eLpNorm_multilinear_four_tendsto_zero: L^4 convergence of each slot with uniform L^4 bounds gives L^1 convergence of any bounded four-linear density, telescoping bound norm_multilinear_four_sub_le + four-factor Hoelder eLpNorm_fourFactor_le; L^4 convergence of k_h and e_h by L^2-L^6 interpolation). The full volume variation is a sum of four such slot terms with permuted vol. Non-vacuity example included (constant fields on [0,1]). weak_palatini_passage_lp states the same five conclusions from the literal hypotheses for cutoff sequences (index N): R_h in Lp(K) converging weakly (every continuous linear functional on Lp converges, WeakStrongPalatiniLebesgue.LpWeakTendsto), with the uniform L^p bound derived by Banach-Steinhaus (lp_norm_bounded_of_weakTendsto), the L^{p'} pairing convergence derived from the Hoelder pairing functional (lpPairingCLM), and the limit L^6 bounds of e and k derived by Fatou (CoframeInterpolation.eLpNorm'_limit_le_of_tendsto_L2); the filter-indexed weak_palatini_passage_with_volume_variation keeps the older rendering (bound + pairings). 'compatible supports' is implicit in working on one finite measure space; the identification of R and the connection-Euler sentence are hypotheses/caveats without formal content.

prop:orlicz.title: A local quartic compactness certificate
prop:orlicz.note: Proved on a bounded four-dimensional region rendered as a coordinate box Q = prod_i (a_i, b_i) of the chart (disclosed rendering: a box is bounded Lipschitz, not smooth; following the campaign guidance the manuscript's test regions are taken as coordinate boxes; the theorems hold for any finite index type, d = 4 included). H^1(Q) is the standard Sobolev space W^{1,2}(Q) (SobolevOpen.MemW12: u in L^2(Q) with weak partials in L^2(Q), tested against real C_c^infty(Q) functions, no boundary condition). orlicz_box: if H_k is bounded in H^1(Q), its test pairings converge (int phi H_k -> int phi H_0 for every phi in C_c^infty(Q); both conditions are implied by H_k -> H_0 weakly in H^1(Q), and neither is the L^2 convergence they produce), H_0 in L^2(Q), and Phi is superlinear (Phi(t)/t -> infinity; monotonicity not needed) with sup_k int_Q Phi(|H_k|^4) < infinity, then H_0 in L^4(Q) and H_k -> H_0 strongly in L^4(Q), full sequence. orlicz_box_of_Lp_bound: the uniform L^{4+delta} clause. orlicz_box_components: multi-component fields (e.g. a Higgs doublet, Orlicz bound on a pointwise norm N_k >= |H_k^c|, Phi monotone). Proof as in the manuscript, with Rellich H^1(Q) compact in L^2(Q) now proved: reflection extension operator W^{1,2}(Q) -> W^{1,2}_c(R^d) (exists_extension_box: even reflection across the 2d faces, weak-derivative identity through the cutoff limit weak_halfspace_limit, then a smooth cutoff), periodisation of compactly supported W^{1,2} functions to the torus with the Fourier rule for weak derivatives (mFourierCoeff_periodize_weak, sobSq_one_periodize), TorusSobolev.rellich_L2, identification of subsequential limits by test pairings (tendsto_L2_box_of_weak), convergence in measure and SuperlinearVitali.tendsto_Lp_of_tendstoInMeasure_of_superlinear. The interior version on arbitrary open sets is also proved (rellich_interior). Non-vacuity: example after memW12_const_box (constant field on the unit box of R^4). Standard axioms only.

prop:sobolev-bosonic.title: A-priori Sobolev bounds imply bosonic strong compactness
prop:sobolev-bosonic.note: PROVED (box rendering of the bounded region K, restriction-space rendering of the fractional spaces): sobolev_bosonic_box_four. K is an open box Q = prod (a_i,b_i) in R^4 and H^s(Q) is the restriction space: a field is bounded in H^s(Q) when it agrees a.e. on Q with the pull-back U o chart of periodic functions U bounded in H^s(T^4) (torus of period L >= max(b_i-a_i), chart x -> (x-a)/L mod Z^4; the classical restriction definition H^s(R^4)|_Q localised, equivalent to the intrinsic norm for Lipschitz regions - this equivalence is not formalised). Hypotheses: e_h bounded in H^{2+sigma}(Q), A_h, H_h bounded in H^{1+sigma}(Q), banks in a compact set (the hypothesis sup||e_h^{-1}||_inf < inf of eq:apriori-bosonic is not needed for these conclusions). Conclusions, along one subsequence: every field is in W^{1,2}(Q) with weak gradient L^{-1}(grad U) o chart (hasWeakPartial_chart: weak derivatives of pull-backs = pull-backs of the Fourier-multiplier derivatives, by Fourier truncation + hasWeakPartial_of_tendsto); e_h -> e in W^{1,2}(Q) and in L^inf(Q); A_h -> A and H_h -> H in W^{1,2}(Q) and L^4(Q); F_{A_h} = dA_h + A_h ^ A_h -> F_A and D_{A_h}H_h = dH_h + rho(A_h)H_h -> D_A H in L^2(Q) (curvature/covariant derivative built from the weak gradients on Q: boxCurv, boxCovD); theta_h -> theta in K_theta; and H_h is uniformly bounded in L^{4+delta}(Q), delta = min sigma 1 (depends only on sigma, d = 4). Ingredients: torus Rellich (rellich_L2_family, torus_extract keeps the regularity of the limits), restriction inequality ||V o chart||_{L^p(Q)} <= L^{4/p}||V||_{L^p(T^4)} (eLpNorm_chart_le), the new fractional embedding H^s(T^d) in L^p for s > d(1/2-1/p), p >= 2 (eLpNorm_le_of_memH_Lp: dyadic blocks 4^k <= <n>^2 < 4^{k+1}, sup <= sqrt(#)||c||_l2, Parseval, Minkowski, geometric sum; on T^4: H^{1+sigma} in L^{4+min sigma 1}), and L^4 x L^4 -> L^2 products. Earlier torus results (sobolev_bosonic_torus etc.) remain as the periodic case. Non-vacuity: example with the constant monomial on the unit box.

prop:dirac-stability.title: Lorentzian Dirac stability produces spinor $H^1$ compactness
prop:dirac-stability.note: Rendering: Sigma = T^3 (fields on R^4 periodic under spatialShift; the paper's Sigma is a general closed 3-manifold), subslab I x Sigma, I=[t0,t1] in (0,T), hypotheses = the ledger encoding DiracStabilityHyp (residual defined by the equation, Hermitian A^mu, A^0>=c, ||A^mu||<=Cb and Cb-Lipschitz on the slab (W^{1,inf}), ||B||<=Cb a.e., spatialH2 (sum_{j<=2}||D^j_y psi(t)||_{L2}) <= Cb, coefficients Cauchy in L^inf, data Cauchy in L^2(cube), residuals Cauchy in L^2(slab)), smooth periodic fields (SmoothFields). PROVED MAIN CONCLUSION: dirac_stability: psi_h Cauchy in C_t L^2_x (sup_t ||psi_m(t)-psi_n(t)||^2_{L^2(T^3)} -> 0), in C_t H^1_x (spatial derivatives, sup in t), and in H^1(I x T^3) (values and all four first derivatives in L^2(I x [0,1)^3)); h1Cauchy_chartBox / diracRoute_spinorH1Cauchy: Cauchy in H^1(Q) on every chart box Q of the subslab, for spinors and dual spinors (SpinorH1Cauchy). Proof exactly as the paper's: L^2 energy inequality for symmetric hyperbolic systems with W^{1,inf} coefficients (l2_energy_estimate: right Dini derivative of E(t)=int Re<w,A^0 w> bounded via frozen-coefficient difference quotients (no derivative of A^0 used) and the Lipschitz commutator lemma -2 int Re<A^j d_j w,w> <= |N|^2 L ||w||^2 (neg_two_integral_ip_pd_le, symmetric difference quotients + translation invariance on the torus), then Gronwall with an L^2_t source), applied to w = psi_m - psi_n with the m-system as principal operator; source = r_m - r_n - B_m w - (B_m-B_n)psi_n - (A_m-A_n)d psi_n with d_t psi_n bounded in L^2 by solving the system (time_bound); H^1 by the interpolation int|d_j g|^2 <= (lam/2) int|d_j d_j g|^2 + (2 lam)^{-1} int|g|^2 (integral_norm_pd_sq_le, integration by parts on the torus) with the uniform H^2 bound; d_t of the difference by solving the system. Note: DiracStabilityHyp does not require measurability of B_h (nor of the residual); the proof handles this by measurable minorants (nrm_le_of_le_add_nonmeas). FINAL CLAUSE PROVED: dirac_limit_equation: with the coefficients explicit (generic hypotheses StabHyp, implied by the bounds of DiracStabilityHyp), B_h L^inf in the paper's sense (AEStronglyMeasurable, bounded) and spatially periodic, and residuals r_h -> 0 in L^2(I x [0,1)^3): on every chart box Q of the subslab, psi_h -> psi in H^1(Q) with psi in H^1(Q) (MemH1: weak gradient g, by SobolevOpen.hasWeakPartial_of_tendsto), A_h^mu -> A^mu uniformly and B_h -> B in L^inf on the slab, and sum_mu A^mu g_mu + B psi = 0 a.e. on Q (the limiting Dirac-Yukawa system; the dual system is the same theorem applied to psibar). Caveat on the ledger encoding: DiracStabilityHyp does not require B_h measurable (its residual norm is then a lower integral); the H^1-Cauchy conclusion holds regardless (measurable-minorant argument), but the limit clause needs the paper's L^inf (measurable) coefficients - without measurability it is false (A^0=1, A^j=0, psi_h=c != 0 constant, B_h=1_V*Id with V = V0 x R^3, V0 subset R of inner measure 0 and full outer measure: all hypotheses hold, eLpNorm r_h = 0, the limit equation fails on V). Rendering Sigma = T^3 as in all ledger encodings of this manuscript (M=(0,T) x T^3).

def:compactness-certificate.title: Classical compactness certificate
def:compactness-certificate.note: Rendering (disclosed, common to the six records): M = (0,T) x T^3 (the paper allows any closed 3-manifold Sigma; its quantitative theorems live on T^3); fields and tests are represented by their spatially Z^3-periodic lifts to R^4 = Fin 4 -> R (cylProj_add_spatialShift: they descend to R x UnitAddTorus (Fin 3)); bundles trivialised ('after fixed local gauge and spin-frame identifications'); flat comparison metric and Lebesgue density; fibres: coframe / metric test Fin 4 -> Fin 4 -> R; ad P = smLie = s(u(3)+u(2)) in the defining 5x5 block representation of G_SM = S(U(3)xU(2)) (skew-Hermitian, block-diagonal, trace 0); Higgs C^2 with rho_H = the u(2) block (Lie-algebra form of the library's higgsRep); spinors C^4 (Weyl basis) tensor a finite fermion-carrier index type C, the chiral bundle cut out by IsChiral / IsCoChiral (left rows carry only the gamma5 = +1 components, right rows only gamma5 = -1; dual spinor opposite); fibre norms are Pi sup norms (equivalent to the fixed bundle metrics). CompactnessCertificate Q z theta, one field per item: (C1) coframes precompact in L^infty(Q), uniformly nondegenerate (|det e_h| >= c > 0 a.e.), bounded in H^1(Q), first-derivative packet with a common compact L^2 screen; (C2) connections precompact in L^4, curvatures bounded in L^2 with a common compact screen; (C3) Higgs bounded in H^1(Q), covariant gradients bounded in L^2 with a common compact screen, and the Orlicz condition: a monotone Phi with Phi(t)/t -> infinity and sup_h int_Q Phi(|H_h|^4) dV_0 < infinity (lower integral of ofReal Phi; equivalent since an increasing Phi is bounded below on [0,infty) and Q is bounded); (C4) SpinorScreenRoute (C4a: Psi, Psibar precompact in L^2, bounded in H^1, first-jet packets with common compact screens) or DiracStabilityRoute (C4b: a compact subslab [t0,t1] x T^3 containing Q, 0 < t0, t1 < T, on which the reconstructed spinors and dual spinors satisfy DiracStabilityHyp = the hypotheses of prop:dirac-stability: first-order systems A^mu d_mu psi + B psi = r (residual defined by the equation, spatially periodic coefficients), Hermitian A^mu (symmetric hyperbolic), A^0 uniformly positive definite, sup_h(||A^mu||_{W^{1,infty}} + ||B||_{L^infty} + ||psi_h||_{L^infty_t H^2_x}) < infinity (B_h in L^infty_{t,x} encoded literally: B_h a.e.-strongly measurable on the slab [t0,t1] x R^3 AND essentially bounded there), coefficients Cauchy in L^infty, initial data psi_h(t0) Cauchy in L^2(T^3), residuals Cauchy in L^2(I x T^3)); (C5) banks in a compact subset of kappa, g_j, lambda_H > 0. Renderings: W^{1,infty} on the slab as 'bounded and Lipschitz' (equivalent on the convex periodic slab); L^infty_t H^2_x as sup over t of sum_{j<=2} ||D^j_y psi(t,.)||_{L^2([0,1)^3)} with classical spatial derivatives (the reconstructions are smooth); 'common compact screen' literally the hypotheses of lem:screen as in def:reduced-certificate (the alternative verification through prop:time-compactness is a sufficient criterion, not a clause). Non-vacuity: flatRegulator_compactnessCertificate (route C4a, every chart); flatRegulator_diracRoute and diracStabilityHyp_zero show route C4b is inhabited. Encoding repair (e31): DiracStabilityHyp now carries the measurability of the zeroth-order coefficients B_h (field: forall n, AEStronglyMeasurable (Bcoef n) (volume.restrict (slab t0 t1))), so the (C4b) route encodes the paper's B_h in L^infty_{t,x} (eq:dirac-uniform) literally; previously only an a.e. bound was required and a non-measurable B made the limit-equation clause of prop:dirac-stability fail. The field is consumed by the Dirac-stability bridge: DiracStab.stabHyp_of_diracStabilityHyp returns it alongside StabHyp, and DiracStab.dirac_stability_limit_equation feeds it to dirac_limit_equation (no separate measurability hypothesis). diracStabilityHyp_zero / flatRegulator_diracRoute updated (constant B = 0 is measurable).

def:strong-packet.title: Classical strong packet
def:strong-packet.note: Rendering (disclosed, common to the six records): M = (0,T) x T^3 (the paper allows any closed 3-manifold Sigma; its quantitative theorems live on T^3); fields and tests are represented by their spatially Z^3-periodic lifts to R^4 = Fin 4 -> R (cylProj_add_spatialShift: they descend to R x UnitAddTorus (Fin 3)); bundles trivialised ('after fixed local gauge and spin-frame identifications'); flat comparison metric and Lebesgue density; fibres: coframe / metric test Fin 4 -> Fin 4 -> R; ad P = smLie = s(u(3)+u(2)) in the defining 5x5 block representation of G_SM = S(U(3)xU(2)) (skew-Hermitian, block-diagonal, trace 0); Higgs C^2 with rho_H = the u(2) block (Lie-algebra form of the library's higgsRep); spinors C^4 (Weyl basis) tensor a finite fermion-carrier index type C, the chiral bundle cut out by IsChiral / IsCoChiral (left rows carry only the gamma5 = +1 components, right rows only gamma5 = -1; dual spinor opposite); fibre norms are Pi sup norms (equivalent to the fixed bundle metrics). StrongPacket z theta L theta0 (RegulatorSequence.HasStrongPacket for the reconstructed fields): on every compact chart (StrongPacketOn, every ChartBox) eq:strong-geometry e_h -> e in L^infty and in H^1 with sup_h(||e_h||_infty + ||e_h^{-1}||_infty) < infinity (coframeInv = pointwise inverse matrix); eq:strong-gauge A_h -> A in L^4 and F_{A_h} -> F_A in L^2; eq:strong-Higgs H_h -> H in L^4 and D_{A_h}H_h -> D_A H in L^2; eq:strong-spinors Psi_h, Psibar_h -> Psi, Psibar strongly in H^1; eq:strong-parameters theta_h -> theta with kappa_h, g_{j,h}, lambda_{H,h} >= c > 0; the limiting coframe lies a.e. in the same orientation / signature chart (coframeChart); the limiting curvature and Higgs derivative are identified weakly with the limit connection (HasWeakCurvature, HasWeakCovGrad: 'not independent weak tensor limits'); limit regularity (H^1 coframe with weak gradient, L^4 smLie-valued A, L^2 F and K, L^4 H, H^1 spinors). 'On every K' is rendered as 'on every chart box' (a compact K is covered by finitely many). Proved relation: StrongPacket.limit_bank_physical (the limiting bank is physical). Non-vacuity: flatRegulator_strongPacket. Not proved (and not immediate): strong packet => reduced convergence, since the strong packet does not place the coframes e_h in a fixed compact subset of the time-oriented chart that def:reduced-topology demands.

thm:certificate-packet.title: Finite certificates produce the classical strong packet

Generic infrastructure in SignedMeasureWeakCompactness.lean: Banach-Alaoglu for finite families, density measures and coefficient replacement, Jordan-decomposition weak-* compactness of bounded signed/vector measures on compact metrizable spaces, weak L^p identification, Radon-Riesz in L^4.

thm:higgs-defect.title: Critical Higgs stress-defect identity
thm:higgs-defect.note: higgs_defect_box (eq:H-defect), higgs_defect_box_einstein (eq:defect-Einstein) and higgs_defect_box_conserved (conservation clause, chart = Q-bar in R^4) prove the theorem on the box; the identified weak gradient limit D_{A_h}H_h -> D_A H is weak L^2(Q) convergence of the realified gradient packet (BoxWeakL2). Box rendering (as for prop:orlicz / prop:covariant-higgs-endpoint): Q = box a b in R^4 with Lebesgue measure, H^1(Q) = W^{1,2}(Q) (SobolevOpen.MemW12), Higgs fields with m complex components assembled into C^m (Hvec); Radon measures live on the closed box Q-bar = Icc a b (functionals on C(Q-bar)) with reference measure Lebesgue on Q pulled back (V0 a b); metrics are continuous fields on Q-bar. eq:critical-Higgs is encoded by H_h, H in W^{1,2}(Q), a uniform W^{1,2}(Q) bound, weak L^2(Q) convergence of components and weak partials (= weak H^1(Q) convergence, componentwise) and a.e. convergence; the uniform L^4(Q) bound is DERIVED from SobolevOpen.exists_sobolev_L4_box (exists_L4_bound_box), so no hypothesis beyond the paper's is used. The L^q (q<4) convergence of eq:critical-Higgs is not needed. Abstract compact-chart versions (with the L^4 bound as an explicit hypothesis) are kept: higgs_defect (eq:H-defect): under uniform metric convergence (nondegenerate), eq:critical-Higgs (H_h -> H a.e., bounded in L^4 -- the explicit Sobolev hypothesis as in lem:critical-cubic), the identified weak gradient limit D_{A_h}H_h -> D_A H weakly in L^2 (realified components) and convergent parameters lambda_h -> lambda, v_h -> v: after extraction the kinetic defect K_H (eq:kinetic-defect) and the quartic measure nu_H >= 0 (eq:quartic-defect) exist and T^H_h dV_{g_h} ->* T^H dV_g + S_H with S_{H,mu nu} = K_{H,mu nu} - lambda g_{mu nu} nu_H (T^H exactly eq:H-stress with V = lambda(|H|^2-v^2)^2; quadratic potential term by weak-L^2 identification, constant term with the volume). higgs_defect_einstein (eq:defect-Einstein): composition with the finite metric equation; hypotheses: Grav_h(k) -> <(Ein+Lambda g)dV_g,k> (gravitational first variation has its intended limit), the remaining stress pairings converge to their regular limits, and the operational residual DS(z_h)[k] = Grav_h(k)/(2 kappa) - (1/2)<T^SM_h dV_{g_h},k> -> 0 (Hilbert convention eq:stress-definition); conclusion Ein(k) = kappa(<T^SM dV_g,k> + <S_H,k>) on every test tensor. higgs_defect_conserved (conservation clause): on a chart K in R^4 with C^1 convergence g_h -> g, total stress T_h = T^H_h dV_{g_h} + R_h uniformly bounded (remaining contributions R_h ->* their regular limit), tested divergence -> 0 (eq:defect-conservation-tested): the limiting stress T^SM dV_g + S_H is conserved and, if the regular stress satisfies its Noether identity, nabla^mu S_{H,mu nu} = 0 (via the proved lem:defect-conservation-transport). The closing remark (conservation does not force S_H = 0) is not formalized.

lem:defect-conservation-transport.title: Covariant conservation under a strong connection limit
lem:defect-conservation-transport.note: Proved on a compact chart K in R^n (Fin n -> R): metrics g_h, g with C^1 components on R^n, C^1 convergence on K (uniform convergence of the components and of all first partials on K), limit g nondegenerate on K; X any C^1 vector field. covSym K g X mu nu is the coordinate formula nabla^{(mu}X^{nu)} = 1/2(g^{mu a}(d_a X^nu + Gamma^nu_{ab} X^b) + (mu<->nu)), Gamma^nu_{ab} = 1/2 g^{nu l}(d_a g_{lb} + d_b g_{la} - d_l g_{ab}), computed in the Banach algebra C(K,R) (inverse metric = matrix inverse over C(K,R)); covSym_apply shows it evaluates at every x in K to the same formula with (g x)^{-1} and the real partials. tendsto_covSym: B_h(X) -> B(X) uniformly on K (det g is a unit of C(K,R), inversion is continuous at units of a complete normed ring, the rest is polynomial). defect_conservation_transport: uniformly bounded, weak-* convergent T_h with sum_{mu nu} T_{h,mu nu}(B_h(X)) -> 0 give sum T_{mu nu}(B(X)) = 0, via |T_h(B_h - B)| <= C ||B_h - B||_inf. defect_conservation_split: T = T_reg + S with the identity for T_reg gives it for S. Renderings disclosed: finite signed Radon measures on the compact chart are encoded by the Riesz identification as continuous linear functionals on C(K,R) (dual norm = total variation, weak-* = convergence against every continuous function on K); metrics are C^1 maps on R^n (only values/first partials on K enter); the uniform inverse bounds on g_h are replaced by nondegeneracy of the limit g on K (which they imply; the g_h are then automatically eventually nondegenerate), symmetry of T and compact support of X are not needed (stronger statement, per C^1 test field).

prop:YM-defect.title: Yang--Mills quadratic stress defect
prop:YM-defect.note: ym_defect: on a compact chart K with finite reference measure V0, continuous symmetric metrics g_h -> g uniformly (all nondegenerate), convergent positive Lie-metric weights (generalizes the fixed metric), and curvatures F_{A_h} -> F_A weakly in L^2 (realified components in an orthonormal basis of the invariant inner product of each simple factor; componentwise weak L^2 is equivalent): after extraction there is a symmetric (S_{mu nu} = S_{nu mu}) tensor-valued finite Radon measure S_YM (Fin 4 -> Fin 4 -> C(K)^*) with T^YM_h dV_{g_h} ->* T^YM dV_g + S_YM (eq:YM-defect; T^YM exactly eq:YM-stress), and strong L^2 curvature convergence gives S_YM = 0. S_YM = B_YM : Q_F is the contraction of the curvature covariance measure (QuadraticPacketDefect.lean: function-level, general-index generalization of lem:positive-packet-defect with positivity on admissible directions) with the uniformly convergent stress coefficients (inverse metric by continuity of inversion in the Banach algebra C(K)). No hypothesis on A_h enters. Fixed signature / uniform inverse bounds beyond nondegeneracy are not used. Non-vacuity example (Minkowski, constant fields).

prop:weak-matter-equations.title: Matter equations survive the bosonic weak limit
prop:weak-matter-equations.note: weak_matter_equations proves the proposition (slab-box rendering of prop:weak-fermion / prop:reduced-continuity: one slab box Q = (t0,t1) x (0,1)^3 containing the time support of the test region K; limit first variations = covector formulas at the limit jet, smLimitVariation / diracLimitVariation). Hypotheses (WeakMatterConvergence, the 'weak Yang-Mills and Higgs class above' plus the proposition's additional ones): coframes with values a.e. in a fixed compact subset of the (oriented, time-oriented) coframe chart and e_h -> e strongly in H^1(Q) (rendering of 'e_h -> e in L^inf cap H^1 with uniformly bounded inverse in compatible spin frames'; L^inf convergence is not needed); A_h -> A in L^4 (ad P-valued limit); F_{A_h} -> F weakly in L^2 (bounded) with F = F_A in D'(Q) (HasWeakCurvature); H_h -> H weakly in H^1(Q); D_{A_h}H_h -> K weakly in L^2 (bounded) with K = D_A H in D'(Q); Psi_h, Psibar_h -> Psi, Psibar weakly in H^1(Q); banks in a compact subset of the physical region converging; Yukawa coefficients converging (as in prop:weak-fermion). 'First-variation consistency and physical stationarity for all matter tests' = RegulatorSequence.MatterConsistent / MatterStationary (eq:C1-consistency and eq:stationarity restricted to matter tests k = 0 of the C^{r0} unit ball; implied by FirstVariationConsistent / PhysicallyStationary: weak_matter_equations_of_regulator). Conclusions: (i) the limiting Yang-Mills, Higgs and Dirac-Yukawa equations hold in distributions: smLimitVariation(v) = 0 for every matter test v in V_K (v = (0,a,0,0,0) YM, (0,0,eta_H,0,0) Higgs, (0,0,0,eta,etabar) Dirac-Yukawa); (ii) the complete fermionic first variation (metric variation through the spin-connection chain included) has its intended limit in the dual norm of V_K^r, r >= 1, with no stress-convergence assumption (diracVariation_weak_tendsto = prop:weak-fermion with A_h -> A, H_h -> H in L^2, the latter by Rellich from weak H^1, weakH1_chart_data). Proof as in the manuscript: on matter tests the bosonic covector is linear in the weak packets (bosonCov_matter: ymWeakCoeff(e,A)[T](F) + higgsWeakCoeff(e,H,A)[T](K) + potStrongCov(e,H)[T]); the coefficients d a + [A_h,a] and d eta + rho_H(a)H_h + rho_H(A_h)eta converge strongly in L^2 (ymWeakCoeff_tendsto, higgsWeakCoeff_tendsto), the cubic force converges strongly in L^1 (critical product L^2 x L^4 x L^4, potStrongCov_tendsto; stronger than the paper's weak L^{4/3}); weak x strong pairings converge uniformly on the C^r unit ball, r >= 2, by the finite-net argument with the full test jet (dual_tendsto_weak_jet, norm_testJet_sub_le); bosonMatterVariation_dual_tendsto + diracVariation_weak_tendsto give smMatterVariation_dual_tendsto; matter_euler_of_residual passes the vanishing matter residual (RegulatorSequence.matter_residual: |DS_SM(z_h)[v]| <= 2c_h + eps_h, the gravitational continuum variation vanishing on matter tests, firstVariation_gravity_matter) to the limit and extends from the unit ball by homogeneity (smLimitVariation_smul). Non-vacuity: the flat regulator satisfies the full hypothesis packet (flatRegulator_weakMatterConvergence, flat_matterConsistent, flat_matterStationary; example). Uses only proved records (prop:weak-fermion, prop:reduced-continuity infrastructure, lem:critical-cubic-type critical product, Rellich/Sobolev on boxes).

lem:positive-packet-defect.title: Covariance measure of a weak quadratic packet
lem:positive-packet-defect.note: Proved for Y_h -> Y weakly in L^2(K, V0; R^r) (WeakTendsto: every continuous linear functional converges), K a compact metric space with any Borel measure V0. positive_packet_defect: there are a subsequence sigma and a matrix-valued measure Q_Y with Y_h (x) Y_h dV0 ->* Y (x) Y dV0 + Q_Y against every continuous coefficient field P in C(K, R^{r x r}) (IsPacketDefect; quadCLM_apply_eq/inner_matAct: the pairing is int sum_ab Y_a P_ab Y_b dV0), Q_Y positive semidefinite and symmetric, |Y_h|^2 dV0 ->* |Y|^2 dV0 + mu_Y with mu_Y = tr Q_Y >= 0, mu_Y = 0 <-> Q_Y = 0 <-> Y_h -> Y in L^2 along the subsequence (eq:positive-defect-equivalence), and for B_h -> B uniformly B_h(Y_h,Y_h) dV0 ->* B(Y,Y) dV0 + B:Q_Y with |B:Q_Y| <= C_B mu_Y, C_B = sup_x ||B(x)||_op (eq:defect-contraction, tested on phi >= 0). Proof: uniform L^2 bound by Banach-Steinhaus; extraction by sequential Banach-Alaoglu in the dual of the separable space C(K, R^{r x r}); positivity by expanding int (Y_h - Y)^T P (Y_h - Y) >= 0 and passing the cross terms by weak convergence (the paper's lower-semicontinuity step); domination by positivity of Q on c I +- B; equivalences via the constant test and the Hilbert identity. Renderings disclosed: matrix-valued Radon measures on the compact domain are encoded (Riesz identification) as continuous linear functionals on C(K, R^{r x r}); PSD = nonnegative on pointwise-PSD continuous fields, symmetric = invariant under transposition, weak-* = convergence against every continuous field (entrywise: P = phi E_ab); the bundle is written in an orthonormal frame as K x R^r (the paper works in a finite atlas; a general metric bundle embeds isometrically in a trivial one over the compact base, and weak L^2 convergence in the subbundle implies it in the trivial bundle); complex packets are covered by realification (R^{2r}); the domination |B:Q| <= C_B mu is stated against nonnegative test functions (equivalent to the total-variation form).

lem:equivariant-tests.title: Equivariant physical tests
lem:equivariant-tests.note: First clause (eq:equivariant-test-invariance) PROVED earlier (equivTestSize_gauge, matrix rendering; see the existing note). Second clause (eq:equivariant-firstvariation-bound) now PROVED: equivariant_firstVariation_bound — for every coefficient bank theta, chart box Q and bounded weak packet z (WeakPacket: e, e^{-1} in L^inf rendered as values a.e. in a fixed compact subset of the coframe chart; e in H^1(Q); A in L^4; F_A in L^2 with F = F_A in D'(Q); H in H^1; D_AH in L^2 identified in D'(Q); Psi, Psibar in H^1) there is C_K < infinity with |DS_theta(z)[v]| <= C_K n_z(v) for every test v (any C^r test space). DS_theta(z) = completeLimitVariation = integral over Q of the complete covector (first-order gravitational representative + Yang-Mills + Higgs + Dirac-Yukawa, i.e. gravCov + bosonCov + diracCov at the jet of the packet, the same covector formulas that define gravLimitVariation / smLimitVariation and that equal the first variation for smooth fields). n_z = covTestSizeSM = ||k||_inf + ||dk||_inf (= ||k||_{W^{1,inf}}) + ||a||_inf + ||eta_H||_inf + ||eta||_inf + ||etabar||_inf + sum_mu (||D_mu a||_2 + ||D_mu eta_H||_2 + ||nabla^{ref,A}_mu eta||_2 + ||nabla^{ref,A}_mu etabar||_2) on Q, with (D_mu a)_nu = d_mu a_nu + [A_mu, a_nu], D_A eta_H = covDerivHiggs, nabla^{ref,A} = d + rho_F(A) (reference spin connection = the flat one of the trivialised comparison geometry, a legitimate choice of the paper's fixed smooth reference connection; another bounded smooth reference changes n_z by an equivalent amount), dual -(.)rho_F(A); fibre sup norms (uniformly equivalent to the Hermitian/Frobenius norms). Explicit constant C_K = ||Lambda_z||_{L^1} + ||Lambda_z o iota_D||_{L^2}(1 + c||A||_{L^2}), Lambda_z the complete covector. Proof = the manuscript's sector estimates: packetCov_mem shows Lambda_z in L^1(Q) (gravity: L^2 coframe derivatives with bounded coefficients; YM/Higgs: F, D_AH in L^2, A, H in L^4; quartic force by H^1 in L^4; Dirac: strong part (de, A, M(H)) x spinor x spinor in L^2 x L^4 x L^4, weak part spinor x spinor gradient) and its restriction to the matter-derivative slots (da, d eta_H, d eta, d etabar) in L^2 (gravCov_iotaD = 0; bosonCov_iotaD: only the YM row pairing F with da and the Higgs row pairing D_AH with d eta_H; diracCov_iotaD: only the kinetic row, spinors in L^4 subset L^2); abs_integral_jet_le (Hoelder L^1 x L^inf + L^2 x L^2 on the jet split); eLpNorm_valPart_le and eLpNorm_derPart_le (raw test derivatives = covariant ones minus zeroth-order connection terms, controlled by ||A||_2 and the sup norms). Renderings: chart box Q (any ChartBox), flat comparison data, trivialised bundles; the two clauses use the matrix rendering (equivTestSize) resp. the field-tuple rendering (covTestSizeSM) of the same eq:equivariant-test-size (the field-tuple one treats a as a one-form). Non-vacuity: flatLimit_weakPacket + example. All cited declarations: standard axioms only.

prop:critical-uhlenbeck.title: Critical Uhlenbeck quotient compactness
prop:critical-uhlenbeck.note: Structural reduction proved; the only gap is the named theorem UhlenbeckSmallEnergyGauge (Uhlenbeck's small-energy Coulomb gauge on Euclidean balls of R^4 for U(m), p = n/2 = 2: energy <= eps_U gives a gauge R, unitary and smooth on the ball, with d^*(R.A) = 0, R.A in W^{1,2}(B_r) with ||R.A||_{W^{1,2}} <= C_r ||F||_2 and the scale-invariant ||R.A||_4 <= C_U ||F||_2), stated as a Prop (a hypothesis of the theorem, not an axiom). critical_uhlenbeck_of_gauge (UhlenbeckSmallEnergyGauge m -> prop:critical-uhlenbeck; box rendering of the chart K = box a b; the reconstructed connections are smooth skew-Hermitian matrix connections A_h; eq:critical-curvature-bound as hypothesis; def:critical-curvature-ui via the ledger encoding CriticalCurvatureUI with |F| the Hermitian norm of all curvature entries): for every compact K' in K and every eta > 0 there is a finite cover of K' by cubes Q_j in K (each inscribed in a small-energy Euclidean ball; the radius comes from uniform integrability, independent of h and of the centre) and cutoff-dependent gauges R_{h,j} with d^*A~_{h,j} = 0 on Q_j, sup_h ||A~_{h,j}||_{W^{1,2}(Q_j)} < infinity (eq:critical-coulomb-bound), ||A~_{h,j}||_{L^4(Q_j)} <= eta (as small as desired after refining), and one subsequence along which, on every Q_j, A~ -> A_j in L^q for all 1 <= q < 4, the gradients converge weakly in L^2 to the weak gradient of A_j in W^{1,2}(Q_j) (weak W^{1,2} convergence), and F_{A~} -> F_{A_j} against every bounded measurable weight (eq:critical-coulomb-convergence; weak L^2 convergence then follows from the uniform L^2 bound on F, which is immediate from the W^{1,2} and L^4 bounds - this last step is not separately formalised). Proved ingredients: w12_compactness_box (Rellich + weak L^2 compactness of the gradients + identification of the weak gradient + Vitali for q < 4), tendsto_integral_curvatureW (strong L^2 x strong L^2 products + weak L^2 derivative part), exists_common_subseq (common extraction over the finite cover). This pass: uhlenbeck_ball_cover (CriticalQuotientDefect.lean) re-derives the cover from the same named theorem keeping the smoothness of the gauges on the balls and using inner cubes of half-side r/4 whose closures lie in the balls (needed to transport matter fields); it is conditional on the same gap.
prop:critical-uhlenbeck.plan: Remaining gap: exactly UhlenbeckSmallEnergyGauge m (K. Uhlenbeck, Comm. Math. Phys. 83 (1982), Thm 1.3, p = 2 in dimension 4): the Neumann/Hodge elliptic estimate ||A||_{W^{1,2}(B)} <= C(||dA||_2 + ||d^*A||_2) for forms with *A|_{dB} = 0, the implicit-function step for the Coulomb condition, and the continuity method along A_t(x) = t A(tx). Research-level elliptic gauge theory; once it is proved (or accepted as a named external theorem), prop:critical-uhlenbeck follows from critical_uhlenbeck_of_gauge with no further work.

lem:critical-positive-graph.title: Positive covariant graph control on a normalized chart
lem:critical-positive-graph.note: Proved in the box rendering of the bounded smooth chart B (as for prop:orlicz / prop:covariant-higgs-endpoint): B = coordinate box Q = box a b in R^4, sections with m complex components u_c in W^{1,2}(Q) = H^1(Q) (SobolevOpen.MemW12; every section smooth up to the boundary is included), connection through matrix entries. The smooth positive-metric reference connection is a skew-Hermitian (metric-compatible) matrix field Gamma with |Gamma_{mu ce}| <= G (smooth on the closure => bounded); the unitary internal representation is a skew-Hermitian matrix field A = rho(A) with entrywise ||A_{mu ce}||_{L^4(Q)} <= M_A (rho linear, so this is equivalent to ||A||_4 <= M_A up to a fixed constant); nabla^{ref,A} u = du + (Gamma + A) u (covD). Norms: ||u||_p := sum_c ||u_c||_p, ||nabla u||_2 := sum_{c,mu} ||(nabla_mu u)_c||_2, ||u_c||_{H^1} = w12Norm (all equivalent to the Hermitian fibre norms up to dimensional constants). critical_positive_graph: there is C (depending only on Q, m, G) such that for every M_A, Gamma, A as above and every u: ||u_c||_4 <= C(||u||_2 + ||nabla^{ref,A}u||_2) (eq:critical-Kato-Sobolev) and ||u_c||_{H^1} <= C(1+M_A)(...) (eq:critical-vector-graph), and the same for every dual section v with the dual connection -(Gamma+A)^T (dualConn; unitary by isSkewHermitianConn_dualConn). The quantifier order (C before Gamma, A) is the gauge-independence clause; no smallness of M_A. Proof exactly as the manuscript: the regularised modulus (|u|^2+eps^2)^{1/2} is W^{1,2} with weak gradient Re<u,du>/(|u|^2+eps^2)^{1/2} (memW12_regMod, via the existing weak chain rule SobolevOpen.MemW12.comp applied to real/imaginary parts), the pointwise Kato identity Re<u,du> = Re<u,nabla u> for skew-Hermitian connections (kato_identity) and Cauchy-Schwarz give |d(|u|^2+eps^2)^{1/2}| <= |nabla_mu u| (kato_regMod), scalar critical Sobolev on the box (exists_sobolev_L4_box) and eps -> 0 give Kato-Sobolev (kato_sobolev_box); then du = nabla u - Gamma u - A u, ||Gamma u||_2 <= G||u||_2, Holder ||A u||_2 <= ||A||_4 ||u||_4 (covariant_graph_box). The Kato inequality is used in the regularised form (the manuscript's eps -> 0 is taken in the Sobolev inequality; the weak gradient of |u| itself is not formalised). Non-vacuity example in KatoInequalitySobolev.lean.

prop:monotonicity.title: A sufficient Euclidean defect-removal mechanism
prop:monotonicity.note: monotone_higgs_defects_vanish proves the whole proposition including the closing sentence. Setting: K compact metric with Borel measure V0; V a real normed space with a continuous linear embedding iota4 : V ->L L^4(K;F) (V into L^4; the L^4 norm in the monotonicity inequality is ||iota4(u-v)||); operators A_h : V -> V' with c1||u-v||^2 + c2||u-v||_4^4 <= <A_h u - A_h v, u-v>; H_h weakly convergent in V (every functional), A_h(H_h) -> J, A_h(H) -> J in V'. Conclusions: H_h -> H in V and in L^4 (tendsto_of_monotone, Banach-Steinhaus boundedness derived). 'V controls the covariant H^1 norm' is rendered as: realified covariant gradients D_h : V ->L L^2(K;R^r) with ||D_h|| <= C_D and D_h H -> D H in L^2 (covers fixed D_A, and A_h -> A in L^4 via ||(D_{A_h}-D_A)u||_2 <= ||A_h-A||_4||u||_4); then Y_h = D_h H_h -> D H in L^2, so (i) the packet defect Q_Y of lem:positive-packet-defect vanishes (eq_zero_iff_tendsto), (ii) every kinetic stress defect K defined by the weak-star relation B_h(Y_h,Y_h) dV0 ->* B(Y,Y) dV0 + K, for continuous coefficient fields B_h -> B uniformly (the components of eq:kinetic-defect with the metric/volume coefficients), is zero (isPacketDefect_zero_of_tendsto + tendsto_contraction + uniqueness of limits), and (iii) the quartic defect nu_H defined by |H_h|^4 rho_h dV0 ->* |H|^4 rho dV0 + nu_H (eq:quartic-defect, volume densities rho_h -> rho uniformly) is zero, via the L^4 -> L^1 estimate || |f_h|^4 - |f|^4 ||_1 <= ||f_h - f||_4 (||f_h||_4 + ||f||_4)^3 (abs_norm_pow_four_sub_le + four-factor Hoelder eLpNorm_fourFactor_le; tendsto_integral_mul_norm_pow_four). The defects are characterised by their defining weak-star relations, so no conclusion of the open records thm:higgs-defect / lem:critical-cubic is assumed (any functional satisfying the defining relation is shown to vanish). Measures are functionals on C(K) as in PositivePacketDefectExact. Non-vacuity example included (V = R, A_h u = 2u).

prop:improvement.title: An assembled strong--weak improvement criterion
prop:improvement.note: PROVED (all clauses). improvement_tendsto (prop:improvement): on a chart rendered as a finite measure space, let (g_h, dg_h) -> (g, dg) in L^inf (g_h -> g in W^{1,inf}) with values of g_h in a fixed compact subset of the nondegenerate set (uniform inverse bounds; fixed signature not needed), dg_h bounded, d^2 g_h -> d^2 g weakly in L^p and bounded (g_h weakly in W^{2,p}), 1/p + 1/p' = 1, p' < inf, and H_h -> H in L^{2p'} (any real inner-product fibre); put f = |H|^2 (normSq_lpTendsto: f_h -> f in L^{p'} by Hoelder). Then for every test tensor with bounded measurable jets (k, dk, d^2k) the assembled pairing int f_h <k, Ein(g_h)> sqrt|g_h| + <(g_h Box - nabla nabla) f_h dV_{g_h}, k> converges to the same expression at the limit, volume densities included. The Hessian term is the distribution defined by its adjoint, <(g Box_g - nabla nabla) f dV_g, k> := int f Hess*_g(k), Hess*_g(k) = d_b d_a S^{ab} + d_l(S^{ab} Gamma^l_{ab}), S^{ab} = sqrt|g|(g^{ab} tr_g k - k^{ab}) (hessAdjJ: chain-rule expansion through the first and second Frechet derivatives of the smooth jet maps sDens and qDens on the nondegenerate set). hessian_consistency: for a smooth metric nondegenerate on the chart R^4, smooth f and smooth compactly supported k, int k^{mu nu}(g_{mu nu} Box_g f - nabla_mu nabla_nu f) sqrt|g| = int f Hess*_g(k) with Hess* on the classical jets (two integrations by parts, SobolevOpen.integral_pd_mul_eq_neg_real; second-order chain rule pd_pd_comp) - so the adjoint definition is the classical one on smooth data. Proof of convergence as in the manuscript: Hess*_g(k) is affine in d^2 g (hessAdjJ_affine) with coefficients continuous on the nondegenerate set (continuousOn_hessCoef0/L); strong L^{p'} coefficients times weak L^p second jets (tendsto_integral_clm_strong_weak) for hessian_product_tendsto, added to einstein_product_tendsto (Einstein product, previous pass). improved_variation_tendsto: if the minimal stress pairings converge and xi_h -> xi, the full improved variation m_h + xi_h * (assembled pairing) converges (closing sentence). Renderings disclosed: finite measure-space chart with fields given by their jets (second jet = weak d^2 g of a W^{2,p} metric; the jets are not required to be derivatives of each other in the convergence theorem, which is therefore more general); tests through bounded measurable jets (includes C_c^inf tests); consistency stated on R^4 with a globally nondegenerate smooth metric. Non-vacuity examples (Minkowski jets) for both theorems.

prop:positive-Higgs-envelope.title: Positive kinetic envelope and the $L^{8/3}$ endpoint
prop:positive-Higgs-envelope.note: All clauses formalised. positive_higgs_envelope (family of cutoffs h, finite cells, packets K h x : D -> F, F a real inner-product space = Higgs fibre with Re of its Hermitian product, comparison c_r|xi|^2 <= r^{mu nu}<xi_mu,xi_nu> <= C_r|xi|^2 with cutoff-independent 0 < c_r <= C_r, masses m >= 0): (1) eq:positive-Higgs-envelope with c_0 = c_r, C_0 = C_r on every cell; (2) the boxed eq:positive-Higgs-L43-L83 as the explicit two-sided bound c_r^{1/2} ||K||_{L_h^{8/3}} <= ||e||_{L_h^{4/3}}^{1/2} <= C_r^{1/2} ||K||_{L_h^{8/3}} (lpNorm_equiv); (3) continuum identification rendered as: for any comparison packet K'_h (the sampled D_{A_h}H_h) the two L_h^{8/3} criteria differ by at most ||K_h - K'_h||_{L_h^{8/3}} (weighted Minkowski, lpNorm83_sub_le), so with a uniformly bounded consistency error (what prop:mesh-consistency supplies on smooth bounded families; that estimate itself is not re-proved here) sup_h ||K_h||_{8/3} < infinity iff sup_h ||K'_h||_{8/3} < infinity. Sharpness (no_automatic_upgrade): on the side-(n+1) unit-box grid with masses h^4 and Euclidean comparison metric, K_h = h^{-7/4} e_0 on one cell has ||K_h||_{L_h^2} -> 0 and ||e_h||_{L_h^1} -> 0 while ||e_h||_{L_h^{4/3}} = h^{-1/2} -> infinity and ||K_h||_{L_h^{8/3}} = h^{-1/4} -> infinity (the discrete form of the paper's Y_n family; the continuum Y_n computation is not separately formalised). Only m_h >= 0 of the mass comparison is used. [Coordinator 30 Sep 2026] Kept open under the corollary policy: the continuum-identification clause uses the estimate of the open prop:mesh-consistency. cor:positive-Higgs-amplitude-criterion.note: positiveHiggs_amplitude_criterion: for any family of finite cell sets, packets K h x : D -> F (F real inner product space = Higgs fibre with Re of its Hermitian product), metrics r h x and masses m h x >= 0, with the lower comparison c_r |xi|^2 <= r^{mu nu} Re<xi_mu, xi_nu> (c_r > 0 cutoff-independent, eq:positive-Higgs-Hodge-comparison), uniform L^1_h and L^inf_h bounds on e_h^{H,+} give uniform L_h^{4/3} bounds on e_h^{H,+} and L_h^{8/3} bounds on |K_h^H| = sqrt(sum_mu |K_mu|^2), norms as in eq:positive-discrete-Lp. lem:SM-descent.title: Descent and covariant Yukawa blocks
lem:SM-descent.note: Descent (sm_descent): the seven rows of tab:SM-representations (Q_L, u_R, d_R, L_L, e_R, optional nu_R, H) are defined on G_SM = S(U(3) x U(2)) as U3 (x) U2, det U2 * U3, U3, (det U2)^{-1} U2, (det U2)^{-1}, 1, U2, and each composed with the covering map (g3,g2,z) -> (z^{-2}g3, z^3 g2) equals the cover representation with its colour/weak factor and U(1) weight 6Y (FaithfulSMQuotient.charged 1/4/-2/-3/-6/0/3); hence the Z_6 generator z6 = (e^{2 pi i/3} I3, -I2, e^{i pi/3}) acts trivially on each row; with smGaugeQuotientEquiv this is descent to the quotient. Yukawa blocks: higgsConj = i sigma_2 conj(H) with higgsConj_mulVec (i sigma_2 conj(UH) = conj(det U) U i sigma_2 conj(H) for U in U(2)); the mass map assembled from Qbar Htilde Y_u u_R + Qbar H Y_d d_R + Lbar H Y_e e_R + h.c. (yukawaMin) and, on the neutral extension, Lbar Htilde Y_nu nu_R + h.c. plus the constant symmetric Majorana block (M_R^T = M_R) on nu_R + nu_R^c (yukawaExt), on the carrier (Q_L + L_L) + (u_R + d_R + e_R) [+ (nu_R + nu_R^c)] tensored with the generation factor C^3; covariance rho(g) M(H) = M(rho_H(g) H) rho(g) for the unitary fermion representation (yukawaMin_covariant, yukawaExt_covariant), hence invariance of the Hermitian mass bilinear Psi^dagger M Psi (bilinear_invariant). Affinity in real Higgs coordinates: M(H) = M(0) + L(H) with L real-linear and M(0) the Majorana block (yukawaExt_affine). eq:yukawa-bound on a bank with all Yukawa/Majorana entries <= R: entries of M(H) <= R(1+|H|), M(H+eta) - M(H) = L(eta) with entries <= R|eta| (yukawa_bound). Renderings: the bound is entrywise (finite-dimensional norm equivalence gives the operator-norm form up to a dimension constant), |H| is the sup norm on C^2; the spacetime-chirality column of the table and the Dirac gamma structure are not part of this internal statement.
