prop:mesh-consistency.title: Smooth local action consistency
prop:mesh-consistency.note: Not closed. Built (e19, sorry-free, standard axioms) the quadrature and pointwise-stencil layers of the paper's proof, in a complete normed real algebra with ||1|| = 1 (represented gauge / spin-gauge algebra) over a normed coordinate space E. (i) Quadrature: LipschitzRiemannSum.norm_riemannSum_sub_integral_le (|h^d sum_k g(kh) - int_[0,1]^d g| <= L h for L-Lipschitz Banach-valued g, sup norm), ..._of_fderiv (C^1: <= B h), norm_perturbed_riemannSum_sub_integral_le (node densities within eps of g: error <= eps + L h; the paper's 'O(h^-4) terms of weight h^4, integrated error O(h)'). (ii) Transport links of eq:lattice-comparison: backwardLink (backward parallel transport from x+he to x = transport of t -> -A(x+(h-t)e)), forwardLink, ring_inverse_backwardLink (its ring inverse is the forward transport; reverse_transport_mul / transport_mul_reverse), first- and second-order edge expansions (norm_transport_sub_linear_le, norm_transport_sub_quadratic_le from the Dyson expansion of PathOrderedExp; norm_backwardLink_sub_le: U_mu(x) = I + h A_mu(x) + O(h^2)). (iii) Four-edge plaquette: norm_linkPlaquette_sub_curvature_le: ||U_mu(x) U_nu(x+he_mu) U_mu(x+he_nu)^-1 U_nu(x)^-1 - (1 + h^2 F_munu(x))|| <= plaquetteConst * h^3, F = d_mu A_nu - d_nu A_mu + [A_mu, A_nu], for A bounded by K with derivative bounded by D and L-Lipschitz (abstract form norm_plaquette_sub_curvature_le from edge Taylor data); norm_linkLogPlaquette_sub_curvature_le: F^h = h^-2 log U_munu = F + O(h) with the analytic series logarithm of ShiftedPlaquette (norm_logOneAdd_sub_le) under the identity-chart smallness (2D + 2K^2 + C) h^2 <= 1/2. (iv) Matter stencils: norm_higgsLink_sub_covDeriv_le (K^h = h^-1(U(x)H(x+he) - H(x)) = dH(e) + A H + O(h)) and norm_spinDifference_sub_covDeriv_le (eq:spin-difference centred covariant difference = nabla Psi + O(h), with U(x-he)^-1 = forward link), for any represented (spin-)gauge connection component A : E -> End F; HiggsPacketConsistency.norm_nativeHiggsPacket_sub_le is the exp-link (native) analogue. All constants explicit in the field bounds. NOT proved: eq:mesh-C1 itself (first-variation consistency |DS_{b,h}[I_h v] - DS_{b,theta_h}(z_h)[v]| <= C_K h of the comparison action) and the strong-packet convergence; see plan. [e29] Added the FIRST-VARIATION layer in the gauge direction (GaugeTheory/TransportGaugeVariation.lean, generic, sorry-free, standard axioms): dual-number transports in D = A[eps]/(eps^2) = TrivSqZeroExt A A (l^1 norm, complete normed real algebra with ||1|| = 1, so every value-level estimate of TransportPlaquetteConsistency applies verbatim in D); hasDerivAt_transport_param: transports of omega + t alpha are differentiable in t at 0 with derivative the eps-part of the dual transport (Gronwall on U_t - U - tV, which solves R' = -(omega + t alpha)R - t^2 alpha V; the paper's 'differentiate the transport equation itself'); hasDerivAt_backwardLink / hasDerivAt_forwardLink: the edge links along A + t a; norm_snd_backwardLink_sub_le: deltaU_mu(x)[a] = h a_mu(x) + O(h^2); hasDerivAt_higgsLink_gauge, norm_higgsLink_gauge_variation_sub_le: deltaK^h[a] = a_mu(x)H(x) + O(h); hasDerivAt_linkPlaquette, norm_snd_linkPlaquette_sub_le: the plaquette after one gauge variation, deltaU_{mu nu}[a] = h^2 deltaF + O(h^3), deltaF = d_mu a_nu - d_nu a_mu + [A_mu,a_nu] + [a_mu,A_nu]. Still NOT proved: eq:mesh-C1 itself and the strong-packet convergence of the reconstruction (see plan). [e34] Unchanged status: the native-route consistency of the UNCHANGED local action is now proved (NativeEulerConsistency.native_consistency, eq:native-consistency, and the generic DiscreteEulerConsistency.norm_eulerRow_sub_contEuler_le for any shifted-first-jet lattice action), but this record concerns the smooth COMPARISON action of app:reconstruction (J_h = rho_h * I_h, lattice transports on J_h f, integrated Palatini density) in the def:regulator encoding (EinsteinSMRegulatorSequence, second-order Scal(g) gravity), which is still not encoded.

lem:native-discrete-KR.title: Discrete translation compactness
lem:native-discrete-KR.note: Proved in the paper's own periodic setting, any dimension d (paper: d = 4), values in any finite-dimensional real (or complex) normed space. Rendering: unit torus 𝕋^d = UnitAddTorus d with Haar probability measure, grid (Z/N)^d, mesh h = 1/N, cells Π_i (g_i/N,(g_i+1)/N], nodal norm ||u||_{2,h} = (N^{-d} Σ|u|^2)^{1/2} (gridNorm), R_h^0 = pcLp; the paper's 2π-periodic box with h = 2π/n differs by a dilation multiplying all L^2 norms by (2π)^{d/2}, so precompactness and vanishing moduli are unchanged; oddness of n is not needed. The family is a sequence u_k on grids N_k -> ∞. Hypotheses: sup_k ||u_k||_{2,h} < ∞ and, for every ε, a ρ such that eventually ||T_{μ,m}u_k - u_k||_{2,h} <= ε for all μ and all integers 0 < m with m h_k <= ρ (positive displacements only; implied by eq:native-discrete-KR). Conclusion: TotallyBounded (range (R^0 u_k)) in L^2(𝕋^d) (= precompact, L^2 complete). Proof as in the paper: exact integer-shift identity R^0u(·+m e_μ/N) = R^0(T_{μ,m}u), isometry of R^0, sub-cell bound ||τ_{θh e_μ}R^0u - R^0u|| <= ||T_{μ,1}u-u||_{2,h} (0<=θ<=1; the paper's exact identity with factor sqrt(θ) is not needed), hence the continuum coordinate modulus <= ||T_{μ,⌊Ns⌋}u-u||_{2,h} + ||T_{μ,1}u-u||_{2,h}; then the new Fréchet–Kolmogorov theorem on 𝕋^d (Fourier proof: ||τ_y f - f||^2 = Σ|e_n(y)-1|^2|f̂(n)|^2, averaging s ∈ [0,δ] in one coordinate bounds the high-frequency tail by the modulus, low modes span a finite-dimensional space; cofinite form for 'eventually in h'; vector values componentwise). Non-vacuity example (constant grid functions) in the file.

lem:native-critical-grid.title: Critical grid bounds and link coefficients

lem:native-reconstruction-identification.title: Identification of raw and trigonometric first jets

lem:native-discrete-Hodge.title: Exact periodic discrete Hodge identity
lem:native-discrete-Hodge.note: periodicHodge_identity: on any finite additive commutative group X (the periodic grid, e.g. (ZMod N)^4) with lattice steps e_mu, directions a finite linearly ordered type (Fin 4), values in a real inner product space (Lie algebra with invariant inner product), and every mesh h, sum_{mu,nu} ||D^+_mu A_nu||^2_{2,h} = ||d_h^+ A||^2_{2,h} + ||delta_h A||^2_{2,h}, with ||u||^2_{2,h} = h^{dim} sum_x |u(x)|^2, D^+ forward difference, delta_h A = -sum_mu D^-_mu A_mu (eq:native-discrete-divergence), ||d^+A||^2 = sum_{mu<nu} ||D^+_mu A_nu - D^+_nu A_mu||^2. Statement: there is eps* > 0 such that for every sequence of grids N_k -> oo and nodal connections with delta_h T A_k = 0 (codiffT = -sum_mu D^-_mu, the paper's eq:native-discrete-divergence), ||T A_{k,mu}||_{4,h} <= eps* and R_h^0 F_h(A_k) -> F strongly in L^2 (F_h = curvLog, the literal logarithmic plaquette), after extraction: R_h^0 A_k -> A strongly in L^4; R_h^0 D+_mu A_{k,nu} -> G_{mu nu} strongly in L^2 with G_{mu nu} = d_mu A_nu (Fourier side, every frequency); for every complex coordinate l of A, l A_nu in H^1 and the trigonometric reconstructions I_h^trig(l A_k) -> l A in H^1; F = F_A pointwise a.e. (F_{mu nu} = d_mu A_nu - d_nu A_mu + [A_mu, A_nu]); delta A = 0 (sum_mu d_mu A_mu = 0 a.e.). Proof as in the manuscript, all clauses formalized: (i) the Lipschitz half of eq:native-YM-envelope, ||N_h(A) - N_h(B)|| <= 5(|W(A)| + |W(B)|)|W(A-B)| pointwise and its L^2_h form (norm_nonlin_sub_le, gridNorm_nonlin_sub_le; from the new Cauchy-estimate Lipschitz bound for the cubic BCH remainder, PlaquetteLogDerivative.norm_bchRem_sub_le); (ii) the absorption inequality eq:native-Coulomb-explicit-absorption with explicit constants (coulomb_absorption: exact Hodge identity + uniform grid Sobolev + envelope), which with B = 0 is the a priori H^1 bound; (iii) discrete Rellich componentwise, L^1 convergence of the nonlinear term and the exact Fourier multipliers of the grid differences identify F = dA + A^A and delta A = 0 on the Fourier side; (iv) comparison fields = Fourier truncations P_R A of the limit (divergence free; P_R A -> A in L^2 and, by the new critical embedding H^1(T^4) c L^4 obtained from the discrete Sobolev inequality by sampling, tendsto_eLpNorm_four_trunc, in L^4; F_{P_R A} -> F), sampled on the grids with fixed-smooth-field consistency; absorption gives limsup_h ||D+A_h - dP_R A||_{L^2} <= c delta_R -> 0, hence the forward differences are Cauchy in L^2 (exists_tendsto_differences); (v) lem:native-reconstruction-identification gives the L^4 and trigonometric H^1 statements and prop:native-YM-identification (first assertion, native_YM_curvature_identification) gives F = F_A pointwise. The convention bridge between CoulombAprioriEstimate/PeriodicForwardDifferenceHodgeIdentityExact (general mesh h, side L = n h, E-valued) and the unit-torus files is NativeCoulombAbsorption (h = 1/N, L = 1, periodicHodgeNormSq = gridNorm^2, gridFwd = DpV, T-read values); the a priori estimate is reproved there in unit-torus notation (coulomb_apriori'). Non-vacuity: example at the end of NativeCoulombCompactness (zero connections in A = C). Standard axioms only.

lem:native-log-gauge-differential.title: Exact logarithmic site-gauge differential
lem:native-log-gauge-differential.note: Both identities proved on the periodic grid (Z/n)^iota (any finite iota, any mesh h != 0), with the gauge group in the units of an arbitrary complete normed real algebra A (nontrivial; for SU(3)xSU(2): pairs of complex matrices) and Lie-algebra fields A_mu(x), xi_x in A, ad_A u = Au - uA. New generic infrastructure (Algebra/MatrixExpDerivative.lean, absent from Mathlib, which differentiates exp only along commuting directions): Duhamel e^A - e^B = int_0^1 e^{sA}(A-B)e^{(1-s)B} ds; D exp(X)[Y] = int_0^1 e^{sX} Y e^{(1-s)X} ds; e^{s ad_X}Y = e^{sX}Y e^{-sX}; int_0^1 e^{sZ} ds = J(Z) = sum Z^k/(k+1)! (OperatorHalfCoth.dexpJ); hence the dexp formula D exp(X)[Y] = (J(ad_X)Y) e^X (fderiv_exp_eq, the paper's left-trivialized U'U^{-1} = h J(Z) A'); strict differentiability with invertible derivative when J(ad_X) is a unit (e.g. ||X|| <= 1/8); every local left inverse Log of exp near X (the logarithm chart) is strictly differentiable at e^X with derivative W -> J(ad_X)^{-1}(W e^{-X}) (hasStrictFDerivAt_log_of_eventually); d/dt Log(e^{t xi} e^X e^{-t eta})|_0 = J(ad_X)^{-1}(xi - e^{ad_X} eta). Gauge application (GaugeTheory/LogarithmicSiteGaugeDifferential.lean): gaugeCurve = A^{q(t)}_mu(x) = h^{-1} Log(e^{t xi_x} e^{hA_mu(x)} e^{-t xi_{x+e_mu}}). gauge_differential (eq:native-gauge-differential): if Log(e^Y) = Y near every h A_mu(x) (any fixed chart containing the scaled links; conjugation invariance not needed) and every J(h ad_{A_mu(x)}) is invertible, then A^{q(0)} = A and d/dt A^{q(t)}_mu(x)|_0 = -K(h ad_{A_mu}) D^+_mu xi(x) - [A_mu(x), m_mu xi(x)], K(Z) = (Z/2)coth(Z/2) = 1/2 J(Z)^{-1}(I + e^Z) (OperatorHalfCoth.halfCoth), via J^{-1}(I - e^Z) = -Z exactly as in the paper. gauge_energy_differential (eq:native-gauge-energy-differential): for any symmetric continuous bilinear form <.,.> on A with <A_mu(x), [A_mu(x), u]> = 0 (implied by ad-invariance + symmetry of the paper's positive invariant metric, e.g. Re tr(X^*Y) with A anti-Hermitian), d/dt 1/2 ||A^{q(t)}||^2_{2,h}|_0 = -<delta_h A, xi>_{2,h}, ||a||^2_{2,h} = h^d sum_{mu,x} <a_mu(x),a_mu(x)>, delta_h A = -sum_mu D^-_mu A_mu; uses <A, K(h ad_A) v> = <A, v> (pairing_halfCoth, the paper's K^*A = A) and summation by parts. Non-vacuity: gauge_hypotheses_nonvacuous (any field with ||h A_mu(x)|| <= 1/8, e.g. A = 0, has invertible J's and a local logarithm chart; exists_log_chart). All cited declarations: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound only.

lem:native-FP-inverse.title: Uniform transverse inverse
lem:native-FP-inverse.note: Proved on the periodic grid (Z/n)^iota with card iota = 4 (any n >= 1, mesh h > 0, side L = n h). Encoding: the Lie algebra is a finite-dimensional nontrivial real inner product space E with an arbitrary continuous bilinear bracket br (invariance of the metric and the Jacobi identity are not needed, so this is more general than the paper); K(Z) = (Z/2)coth(Z/2) is encoded through the paper identity K(Z) = 1/2 J(Z)^{-1}(I + e^Z) with J(Z) = sum_k Z^k/(k+1)! = int_0^1 e^{tZ} dt (eq:native-JK; OperatorHalfCoth.halfCoth, an analytic function, Z J(Z) = e^Z - 1 (mul_dexpJ), scalar check halfCoth z (e^z - 1) = (z/2)(e^z + 1) (halfCoth_real_mul), K(0) = I, ||K(Z) - I|| <= 12||Z||^2 on ||Z|| <= 1/4 (norm_halfCoth_sub_one_le)); M_A xi = delta_h(K(h ad_{A_mu}) D^+_mu xi + [A_mu, m_mu xi]) with delta_h = -sum D^-_mu (FaddeevPopov.fpOp, eq:native-FP). With r_FP = 1/(64(||br||+1)), independent of n and h, and the hypothesis ||A_mu||_{4,h} < r_FP for every direction mu (implied by the paper hypothesis ||A||_{4,h} < r_FP for the pointwise norm): fp_coercive: <M_A xi, xi>_{2,h} >= 1/2 ||D^+ xi||^2_{2,h} on the mean-zero space Z_h (eq:native-FP-coercivity; proof as in the paper: h||A||_inf <= ||A||_{4,h}, ||K - I|| <= C h^2|A|^2, weighted Hoelder L^4 x L^4 x L^2, ||m xi||_4 <= ||xi||_4, mean-zero Sobolev grid_sobolev_poincare_meanZero_l2); fp_bijective: M_A : Z_h -> Z_h bijective (exists unique mean-zero solution); fp_dual_inverse_sSup: ||D^+ M_A^{-1} f||_{2,h} <= 2 ||f||_{H^{-1}_h} with the dual norm defined as the sSup over mean-zero zeta with ||D^+ zeta||_{2,h} = 1 (dualNorm, abs_gridInner_le_dualNorm) (eq:native-FP-dual-inverse); fp_divergence_inverse: ||M_A^{-1} delta_h R||_{2,h} + ||M_A^{-1} delta_h R||_{4,h} + ||D^+ M_A^{-1} delta_h R||_{2,h} <= (2 + 2 sqrt2 L + 4(3 + 2 sqrt2)) ||R||_{2,h} (eq:native-FP-divergence-inverse; constant independent of n for the fixed box L = 2 pi); fp_inverse_contDiffOn: on {A : ||A_mu||_{4,h} < r_FP} the extension N_A xi = M_A(xi - mean xi) + mean xi is invertible, A -> N_A^{-1} is C^k for every k (smooth and analytic orders), and N_A^{-1} f is the mean-zero solution of M_A xi = f for mean-zero f (smooth dependence of the inverse). Non-vacuity: example with A = 0 (M_0 = delta_h D^+). No self-adjointness of M_A is used. All cited declarations use only propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound.

thm:finite-Coulomb-normalization.title: Finite critical Coulomb normalization
thm:finite-Coulomb-normalization.note: Proved for the paper's exact gauge group G_SM = S(U(3)xU(2)) (eq:gauge-group): StandardModelCoulomb.finite_coulomb_normalization_SM. Setting: 4D periodic grid (ZMod n)^iota, card iota = 4, mesh h, box side L = n h GENERAL (the paper fixes L = 2pi; constants depend only on L and the group/metric, never on n or h); A_SM = M3(C) x M2(C) with operator norms, invariant Frobenius metric Re tr(X3^*Y3) + Re tr(X2^*Y2) (toESM). Statement: for every eps_* > 0 there are eps_c, C_c > 0 such that every g_SM-valued seed B (skew-Hermitian blocks, tr B3 + tr B2 = 0) with ||B||_{4,h} + ||F_h(B)||_{2,h} <= eps_c admits a site gauge q with q_x in S(U(3)xU(2)) (unitary, det q3 * det q2 = 1) such that A = h^-1 Log(q_x e^{hB} q_{x+mu}^*) (linkA h B 1 q; FiniteCoulomb.linkA_at_one) is g_SM-valued (skew, tr A3 + tr A2 = 0), delta_h A = 0, ||A||_{1,h} + ||A||_{4,h} <= C_c(||B||_{2,h} + ||F_h(B)||_{2,h} + ||B||_{4,h}^2) and ||A||_{4,h} <= eps_*. NORM CONVENTION (disclosed): ||A||_{4,h} := sum_mu ||A_mu||_{4,h} (equivalent within fixed factors to the l4 combination of the components), ||A||_{2,h}^2 = sum_mu ||A_mu||_{2,h}^2, ||A||_{1,h} as in lem:native-reconstruction-identification, ||F||_{2,h} over mu<nu. Proof: general theorem FiniteCoulomb.finite_coulomb_normalization (unitary group of any finite-dim C*-algebra with invariant metric; the paper's homotopy ODE q' = xi q, xi = M_{A_s}^-1 delta_h R_s, Coulomb preservation, L^2 energy bound, curvature covariance + exact split, a priori a <= C_0 b + C_1 a^2, first exit, global existence via ODEContinuation.exists_solution_of_apriori); trace constraint along the path (CoulombTrace.trace_linkA_of_solution with tau = Re/Im(tr3 + tr2)) gives tr A3 + tr A2 = 0; then det(e^{hA}) = e^{tau(hA)} = 1 (MatrixDetExp.det_exp_eq_complex_exp_trace) on every link gives chi(q_x) chi(q_{x+mu})^* = 1 for chi = det3*det2, so chi(q) is a constant unit d, and the constant central phase c (c^5 = d^-1) gives the gauge c q in S(U(3)xU(2)) with the same links (the determinant clause is obtained by this post-hoc central correction rather than a Liouville ODE along the path; same conclusion). Also: U(N) (FrobeniusCoulomb), SU(N) (SpecialUnitaryCoulomb), general trace-constrained version (CoulombTrace); non-vacuity: FrobeniusCoulomb.exists_coulomb_zero_seed. Log = analytic series branch near 1 (conjugation-invariant chart).

lem:determinant-screen-flux.title: Determinant compactness, admissibility, and flux
lem:determinant-screen-flux.note: All clauses proved (determinant_screen_flux) on the paper's periodic box of side L > 0 (2 pi in the paper), four-dimensional grids (Z/n_k)^4 with n_k -> infinity, h_k = L/n_k (oddness not needed). Hypotheses (structure CurvatureScreen, exactly the lemma's): G_SM links U_k; for every oriented pair mu<nu an arbitrary logarithm L_k(x,mu,nu) of the full plaquette (exp in both factors = P_{U,mu nu}(x); no chart and no bound on link logarithms assumed); literal full curvature packet F_k = (h^-2 L_k)_{mu<nu} bounded in L^2_h; full-box adjoint Wilson screen lim_{rho->0} limsup_k Omega_h(F;rho) = 0 used for positive displacements m h <= rho (implied by the paper's |m| h <= rho). Norm rendering: operator (unitarily invariant) norm on each matrix factor, max norm on pairs and on the six-component packet; equivalent to the invariant Euclidean metric up to a dimensional constant (boundedness/vanishing moduli unchanged); Ad acts by linear isometries (adPair, adPacket). Conclusions: (1) eventually f_h = l_c(F_h) exactly (eventually_detPacket; via eventual uniform smallness of h^2 F_h = L_h (eventually_small: scalar-magnitude uniform integrability from the proved thm:native-Wilson-compactness, exists_tail_le and the cell mass h^4) and DeterminantFlux.ellC_eq_arg_smChi); (2) eventually ||T_{mu,m} f - f||_{2,h} <= 2 ||W_{mu,m} F - F||_{2,h} for all mu, m >= 0 (Ad-invariance of l_c, ellC_openLink; |l_c| <= 2||.||), hence omega_h(f;rho) <= 2 Omega_h(F;rho) (negative ordinary shifts have the same norms by translation invariance); (3) max_{x,mu,nu} |phi_{mu nu,h}(x)| -> 0 (all ordered pairs, via abPhase_swap/abPhase_self); (4) R_h^0 f_h precompact in L^2 (TotallyBounded, unit-torus rendering of native_discrete_KR as for lem:native-discrete-KR); (5) eventually d_h f_h = 0 exactly (all cube sums vanish); (6) every coordinate-plane flux is 2 pi m, m integer (all k); eventually base-point independent, mean curvature L^-4 h^4 sum f = 2 pi m / L^2 and 2 pi |m| <= ||f_{mu nu}||_{2,h} (from determinant_screen_flux_exact / mean_curvature_eq_flux / two_pi_abs_flux_le); (7) the integer vectors (m_{mu nu,h})_{mu<nu} are bounded (2 pi |m| <= ||f|| <= 2||F||) and constant along a strictly increasing subsequence (pigeonhole, Finite.exists_infinite_fiber). Non-vacuity: curvatureScreen_trivial (trivial links, zero logarithms). Also closes prop:native-determinant-split (extra key, see there). All cited new declarations: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound only.

lem:determinant-Hodge-stability.title: Strong stability of the periodic discrete Hodge inverse

Finite identities and uniform bounds of eq:determinant-Hodge-bounds: GridHodge.hodge_stability_exact, hodge_stability_bounds (previous pass; closed zero-mean real two-form, d_h a0 = f, delta_h a0 = 0, mean zero, ||D+a0||_{2,h} = ||f||_{2,h}, L^-1||a0||_{2,h} + ||a0||_{4,h} <= (6+5 sqrt 2)||f||_{2,h} in four dimensions). Strong-convergence clause (this pass; unit-torus rendering, mesh h = 1/N - the paper's box is its dilation, and scaledPrimitive is linear so constant rescalings commute; real forms complexified by realC): if the zero-mean real two-forms f_h satisfy R_h^0 f_h -> F strongly in L^2 (componentwise), then for a0_h = delta_h Delta_h^dagger f_h = GridHodge.scaledPrimitive (1/N) f_h: R_h^0 a0_h -> a0 = delta Delta^dagger F strongly in L^2 (contPrimitive, the Fourier form a0^_nu(m) = sum_kappa conj(2 pi i m_kappa) F^_{kappa nu}(m)/(4 pi^2|m|^2)), a0 in H^1 and R_h^0 D+_mu a0_h -> d_mu a0 (weak derivative) strongly in L^2, I_h^trig a0_h -> a0 strongly in H^1 (hodge_strong_convergence, any dimension), and in four dimensions R_h^0 a0_h -> a0 strongly in L^4 (hodge_strong_convergence_four). prop:periodic-determinant-normalization.title: Zero-flux Abelian normalization with unrestricted flat holonomy
prop:periodic-determinant-normalization.note: Clause-level status: ALL CLAUSES PROVED. Exact part (previous pass): DeterminantFlux.periodic_determinant_normalization_exact (potential a0 = delta_h Delta_h^dagger f, constants with L c_mu in (-pi, pi] equal to the principal arguments of the cycle holonomies of the flat residual, periodic site gauge, delta_h(a0 + c) = 0; no smallness of f, a0 or cycle phases used) and, for screened sequences, DeterminantScreenFlux.native_determinant_split. lem:flat-semisimple-normalization.title: Flat semisimple normalization without a small-holonomy assumption
lem:flat-semisimple-normalization.note: Proved on the periodic four-dimensional grid (Z/n)^4 (any n >= 1, mesh h > 0, box side L = n h), G_ss = SU(3) x SU(2) (Gss). Flatness: every oriented plaquette trivial, V_mu(x)V_nu(x+mu) = V_nu(x)V_mu(x+nu) (IsFlat). Part A (any group): ladder lemmas (plaquette moves along lines and staircases), flatness implies the based cycle holonomies w_mu = V_mu(0)V_mu(e_mu)...V_mu((n-1)e_mu) commute (cycle_commute); flat_gauge_equiv: two flat periodic fields with equal based cycle holonomies are gauge equivalent by the explicit site gauge g_x = P_W(x)^-1 P_V(x) comparing staircase path transports from the root (exactly the paper's argument: plaquette moves preserve the comparison, equal cycle holonomies make it periodic; no pointwise-ratio flatness assumed); flat_gauge_eq_const for constant commuting targets. Part B (no simultaneous spectral theorem needed): a common eigenvector of finitely many commuting complex operators (exists_common_eigenvector, by invariant-subspace induction); for commuting U_mu in SU(N): b_mu = cfc(i arg)(U_mu) - 2 pi i k_mu P with P the rank-one projector onto a common eigenvector, k_mu = tr(cfc(i arg)U_mu)/(2 pi i) in Z (det exp = exp tr), giving pairwise commuting, anti-Hermitian, traceless logarithms with e^{b_mu} = U_mu and ||b_mu|| <= (N+1) pi (operator norm) (exists_commuting_logs) -- this is the paper's 'subtract 2 pi m from one eigenangle' rendered via the common eigenvector. Assembly flat_semisimple_normalization: V flat => there are commuting b_mu = (b^3_mu, b^2_mu) in su(3)+su(2) (anti-Hermitian, traceless), entrywise |b_mu(i,j)| <= 4 pi / L uniformly, with cycle holonomies e^{L b_mu} equal to those of V, and an SU(3)xSU(2) site gauge g with g_x V_mu(x) g_{x+mu}^-1 = e^{h b_mu} for all x, mu; no smallness of the holonomies. flat_semisimple_normalization_seq: for grids n_k with fixed L = n_k h_k, the bounds are uniform in k and after extraction the constant coordinates converge (constant_coordinates_subseq, Bolzano-Weierstrass); constant coordinates have identically zero first differences and constant commuting links have trivial plaquettes (plaq_const_eq_one), hence zero curvature. Non-vacuity: isFlat_one. Axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound only.

cor:determinant-resolved-closure.title: Determinant-resolved finite Wilson closure

lem:covariant-quadrature.title: Covariant cell-average quadrature
lem:covariant-quadrature.note: Proved (e19). Setting: metric connection D = d + omega on the trivialised bundle [0,1]^d x V, V a real Hilbert space (the manuscript's finite direct sum of test fibres), omega : R^d -> L(R^d, End V) with skew-adjoint values (IsMetric), covariant derivative covDeriv omega X x = dX(x) + omega(x)(.) X(x); uniform grid of mesh h = 1/M with cells C_x = x + [0,h)^d (UnitCubeRiemannSum.cell); P_{x<-y} the parallel transport (PathOrderedExp.IsTransport: P' = -omega(gamma)(gamma') P, P(0) = 1) along a path gamma_{x,y} from y to the node x; Q_h v(x) = h^-d int_{C_x} P_{x<-y} v(y) dy (cellAverage, eq:covariant-test-average). (a) abs_covariant_quadrature_sub_le (eq:covariant-quadrature): for any path family with speed <= l, a measurable transport field y -> P_{x<-y}, X continuous on the cube and differentiable along the paths with ||DX|| <= B there, and integrable v: |h^d sum_x <X(x), Q_h v(x)> - int <X, v>| <= l B ||v||_{L^1}; the proof is the paper's (metric compatibility makes transports isometries, inner_transport_apply_apply; covariant FTC along the path, abs_inner_covariant_ftc: |<X(x), P_{x<-y} w> - <X(y), w>| <= B l ||w||). (b) abs_covariant_quadrature_straight_sub_le: the concrete family of straight segments inside the cell (length < h in the sup norm, so C = 1) for omega bounded and Lipschitz on the cube; existence of the transports by gluing short Picard-Lindelof pieces (exists_transport_of_le) and Lipschitz dependence on y by Gronwall (norm_straightTransport_sub_le), so the measurability hypothesis is discharged. (c) Norm bounds: norm_cellAverage_le (||Q_h v||_{inf,h} <= ||v||_inf, with a pointwise bound on the cell) and cellAverage_sq_sum_le (h^d sum_x ||Q_h v(x)||^2 <= int ||v||^2, Cauchy-Schwarz on each cell, sq_setIntegral_le_mul); straight_cellAverage_norm_bounds packages both for the straight family. (d) Equivariance: isTransport_gaugeTransform (endpoint transformation: g(gamma t) P(t) g(gamma 0)^-1 is the transport of omega^g = g omega g^-1 - (dg) g^-1), cellAverage_gaugeTransform (Q'_h(g v) = g Q_h v) and inner_cellAverage_gaugeTransform (both sides of eq:covariant-quadrature unchanged under unitary frame changes, LinearIsometryEquiv-valued g). Disclosed renderings: buffered chart = unit cube (any coordinate box is an affine image); trivialised bundle (fixed local frames, as in the manuscript); lengths and operator norms in the sup norm of R^d (other norms change C by a dimensional factor); 'a fixed family of paths' = a path family with measurable transport field (automatic for the straight family). Non-vacuity: flat-connection example at the end of the file.

prop:Wilson-packet-transfer.title: Finite packet and open-link transfer

lem:translation-Kato.title: Translation Kato inequality
lem:translation-Kato.note: translation_kato: for a Hilbert fibre H over R or C, any representation rho : G -> H ->L H with values in unitary (H ->L H), parallel transports P x : G and displacement a (= s e_mu) in an additive group of points, | |Y(x+a)| - |Y(x)| | <= |T Y(x) - Y(x)| with T Y(x) = rho(P x)(Y(x+a)) (eq:continuum-covariant-translation). The 'thus' clause: translation_kato_eLpNorm (the L^p, in particular L^2, ordinary translation modulus of |Y| is bounded by the covariant one, any measure) and translation_kato_modulus_tendsto (vanishing covariant modulus forces vanishing ordinary modulus).

lem:compact-magnitude-ui.title: Compact scalar magnitude implies energy uniform integrability
lem:compact-magnitude-ui.note: Proved. For a family F : ι → Lp V 2 (μ.restrict K) (V any normed group) that is relatively compact (compactMagnitude_ui_of_isCompact_closure: IsCompact (closure (range F))) or totally bounded (compactMagnitude_ui), eq:compact-magnitude-ui holds in the form CriticalCurvatureUI μ K F of Continuum/CriticalCurvatureUniformIntegrabilityExact.lean: sup_f sup_{E ⊆ K measurable, μ E ≤ δ} ∫⁻_E ‖f‖² → 0 as δ ↓ 0. Proof as in the paper: finite L² net of radius ε/2, MeasureTheory.unifIntegrable_finite for the net (absolute continuity), and the triangle inequality ‖1_E f‖₂ ≤ ‖f − f_j‖₂ + ‖1_E f_j‖₂ (compactMagnitude_unifIntegrable gives UnifIntegrable F 2 μ in Mathlib's sense). prop:Wilson-screen-compactness.note: PROVED (e28), all three assertions, unit-torus rendering of the periodic comparison box (as for thm:native-Wilson-compactness): the chart B is an open subset of T^d = UnitAddTorus d (any finite d) with Haar probability measure, coordinate displacements t -> t + coordPt mu s. Hypotheses exactly the paper's: Y_h bounded in L^2(B) (a.e.-strongly measurable on the box) and eq:Wilson-continuum-screen (CovScreen: on every compact K in B, for every eps a delta with, cofinitely in h, ||T_{mu,s}Y_h - Y_h||_{L^2(K)} <= eps for all mu and 0 <= s <= delta; only positive displacements are used). Conclusions: (i) |Y_h| relatively compact in L^2_loc(B) (wilson_screen_magnitude_nets: on every compact K in B finite eps-nets in L^2(K) drawn from the family; equivalent total-boundedness form LocalKRTorus.totallyBounded_of_nets), via the translation Kato inequality (lem:translation-Kato, translation_kato_of_isometry) and the new LOCAL Kolmogorov-Riesz theorem LocalKRTorus.exists_net_of_local_modulus (Lipschitz cutoff chi = max(0,1-dist(.,K)/r) with cthickening 3r K in B, translation modulus of chi f bounded by the local modulus on cthickening 2r K plus (s/r)||f||, torus Kolmogorov-Riesz kolmogorovRiesz_torus_vector_cofinite); (ii) |Y_h|^2 uniformly integrable on every compact K in B (wilson_screen_magnitude_ui: for every eps a delta with ||Y_h||_{L^2(E)} <= eps for all h and measurable E in K with |E| <= delta), via lem:compact-magnitude-ui (compactMagnitude_ui, proved); (iii) vector part (wilson_screen_vector_nets): if the transports are the unitary parallel transports of continuous represented connections a_h (IsUnitaryTransport: rho(P) is the two-sided inverse of the unitary forward transport of tau -> a_h(t + tau e_mu)) with sup_h ||a_h||_{L^4(B)} <= M_A (eq:critical-A4-bound, connections in the normalized local gauge), then Y_h itself is relatively compact in L^2_loc(B). Proof as the paper: eq:short-line-integral ||rho(P)-I|| <= min(2, int_0^s |a(t+tau e)|) (IsUnitaryTransport.norm_sub_one_le, from the integral equation and unitarity), Fubini |int_K L_s| <= s ||a||_{L^1(K'')} <= s M_A (Holder L^4 -> L^1 on the probability torus), Chebyshev |{L_s > delta}| <= s M_A/delta, uniform integrability (ii) on the translated exceptional set, continuity of the transports in the base point (Gronwall + uniform continuity) for measurability, then local Kolmogorov-Riesz.

lem:critical-Coulomb-Hodge.title: Critical Coulomb Hodge absorption
lem:critical-Coulomb-Hodge.note: Proved in the box rendering (as for prop:orlicz): the small-energy Coulomb ball B is a coordinate box Q = box a b in R^4, and B' compactly contained in B is rendered by an arbitrary compact K in Q (L^4(K) convergence for every compact K covers every B' with closure in B). Connections: m x m complex-matrix-valued one-forms with entries A_h nu c e in W^{1,2}(Q) (implicit in the lemma: the Coulomb representatives of prop:critical-uhlenbeck are W^{1,2}; needed to make d^*A and F_A functions; no uniform W^{1,2} bound is assumed), co-closed = sum_mu d_mu A_mu = 0 a.e. on Q, F = dA + [A ^ A] entrywise from the weak gradients (curvatureW), L^p norms entrywise. critical_coulomb_hodge_box: there is delta_0 > 0 depending ONLY on the dimension and m (not on Q or on the cutoff; delta_0 = (2 kappa + 1)^{-1}, kappa = coulombKappa built from Mathlib's Gagliardo-Nirenberg-Sobolev constant) such that if all L^4(Q) entry norms of A_h and A are <= delta <= delta_0 ('uniformly sufficiently small'), A_h -> A in L^2(Q) and F_{A_h} -> F_A in L^2(Q), then A_h -> A in L^4(K) for every compact K in Q (eq:critical-A4-strong). Proof as in the manuscript: chi in C_c^infty(Q), chi = 1 near K; compactly supported Hodge estimate for chi a_h (flat Weitzenboeck identity ||grad w||^2 = 1/2 sum ||(dw)_{mu nu}||^2 + ||d^*w||^2 for compactly supported W^{1,2} one-forms, weitzenbock_flat, proved by periodisation to the flat torus, the Fourier rule for weak derivatives and a Lagrange identity on every Fourier mode) and critical Sobolev H^1_c -> L^4; d^*(chi a_h) is of order zero by co-closedness (eLpNorm_div_cutoff_le); d(chi a_h) = chi(F_{A_h} - F_A) - ([chi a, A_h] + [A, chi a]) + dchi ^ a_h (curl_cutoff_eq); absorption of the delta-terms when kappa delta <= 1/2 (coulomb_hodge_step). Non-vacuity example in CriticalGaugeEstimates.lean.

prop:native-consistency.title: Growing-band consistency of the unchanged finite action
prop:native-consistency.note: PROVED (e34, sorry-free, standard axioms). Both clauses. Setting: the unchanged local action S_h^loc = NativeDensity.localAction (all four rows of eq:native-densities: literal Cartan plaquette logarithm, gauge plaquettes, Higgs links, Dirac links) on the periodic grid (Z/n)^4 with mesh h; a smooth field tuple y : R^4 -> (e, A, H, Psi, Psibar) of period n h (the paper's periodic comparison box), sampled at the nodes (samp). Raw Euler row E_h^raw(y)(x) = h^-4 d_{y(x)} S_h^loc (DiscreteEulerConsistency.eulerRow, = eq:raw-euler-row in covector form). Continuum Euler density E_0 = Euler-Lagrange expression d_w L_0 - sum_mu d_mu d_{p_mu} L_0 (contEuler) of the continuum Lagrangian L_0(w,p) = F^(1)(0; w,...,w; p,...,p) (limDensity of the first-jet density of lem:native-firstjet-normal-form), identified sectorwise (limDensity_firstJetDensity_eq, nuFieldStrength_cont: F = dA - dA + [A,A]; nuHiggsLinkJet_cont: D_A H = dH + rho_H(A)H; nuDiracDiffJet_cont / nuDiracDiffBarJet_cont: spin-covariant derivatives with the torsion-free reader connection omega(e, de) and rho_S(A); gravity = first-order Palatini representative NativeGravityJet.palatiniFirstOrder, the convention of prop:native-gravity-firstjet; its Euler expression equals that of any density differing by a divergence). (1) eq:native-consistency = NativeEulerConsistency.native_consistency: for a compact coframe chart K_e in {det > 0} (uniform inverse metric), amplitude bound A and band constant B there are C and c_res > 0 such that for all K >= 1, h > 0 with hK <= c_res, all n and every C^3 field of period nh with coframe values in K_e, |y| <= A and ||D^j y|| <= B K^j (j = 1,2,3; eq:growing-derivatives at the orders used, q >= 5 only strengthens it), the samples lie on the oriented and Cartan-logarithm charts and ||E_h^raw(S_h y)(x) - E_0(y)(h x)|| <= C h K^3 at EVERY node. Proof = the paper's: exact jet scaling F^(1)(h,(v,Kq)) = K^2 G(K^-1, hK, (v,q)) (firstJetDensity_jetScale, lem:native-scaling on first jets, all four sectors) with G smooth at rho = 0 for every nu (contDiffAt_scaledDensity), uniform C^3 bounds on compact parameter/jet sets (exists_densityReg), the generic discrete-to-continuum Euler consistency of shifted-first-jet actions (norm_eulerRow_sub_contEuler_le: explicit discrete summation by parts eulerRow_action_eq, Taylor expansion of shifted stencils and of the divided difference of D_dF using symmetry of D^2 y, constant eulerConst independent of h, n and the field), and the exact rescalings of the raw row (eulerRow_smul_action) and of E_0 (contEuler_scale). (2) eq:native-Cartan = native_cartan_consistency: ||R^h_{mu nu}(x) - R_{mu nu}(z)|| <= C h K^3 for every node x and EVERY z in its cell (||z - h x|| <= h), R = d omega + omega wedge omega of the torsion-free reader connection omega_mu = e Gamma_mu e^-1 - d_mu e e^-1 (contCartan), which equals the Riemann tensor of g = e^T eta e in mixed frame/coordinate components e Riem_{mu nu}(g) e^-1 (contCartan_eq_riem: the Cartan structure equation, proved; riemMat = d_mu Gamma_nu - d_nu Gamma_mu + [Gamma_mu, Gamma_nu] with the Christoffel symbols readerGamma of g); native_cartan_riem states the clause directly against e Riem(g) e^-1. This is an L^infty bound for the piecewise-constant reconstruction, hence the L^2(Q) bound with factor |Q|^(1/2). Disclosed: finite-dimensional gauge algebra and Higgs/spinor fibres (FiniteDimensional, as in the paper); trivialised bundles, one fixed frame; sup norms on R^4 (other norms change C by dimensional factors); readerGamma is the Christoffel formula with dg = (de)^T eta e + e^T eta de (NativeScaling.readerG, product rule; not re-derived against Gravity/CoordinateCurvature.lean). Non-vacuity: example (flat constant field satisfies the packet). Fixed-scale corollary: native_sigma_of_solution.

lem:native-plaquette.title: Regularity of the plaquette map
lem:native-plaquette.note: Proved in a real Banach algebra 𝔄 with ‖1‖ = 1 (NormOneClass; scoped hypothesis, as in the previous partial), for X, Y, a, b in 𝔄. Bundled statement exists_joint_analytic_extension: there is Φ : ℝ × 𝔄⁴ → 𝔄 (jointLogPlaquette) with (i) Φ analytic at every (0, X, Y, a, b), (ii) Φ(0; X,Y,a,b) = a - b + [X,Y], (iii) h² Φ(h) = log(e^{hX} e^{h(Y+ha)} e^{-h(X+hb)} e^{-hY}) for all h ≠ 0 with the series logarithm log(1+z) = z Σ (-1)^n z^n/(n+1), and (iv) for every order k and every compact set K of parameters there are h₀ > 0 and C with ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ k Φ (h, q)‖ ≤ C for |h| ≤ h₀ and q ∈ K, i.e. all fixed-order derivatives in h and in the parameters are uniformly bounded on compact argument sets for small h (second sentence of the lemma). The 'analytic branch' is identified: exp(log(1+z)) = 1 + z for ‖z‖ < 1 (exp_logOneAdd, proved by differentiating t ↦ exp(-log(1+tz))(1+tz) with a Commute-based derivative of exp, no commutativity of 𝔄 needed), hence exp(h² Φ(h)) = P(h) whenever ‖P(h) - 1‖ < 1 (exp_sq_smul_logPlaquette). Method for (i)/(iv): exp u = 1 + u + u² E(u) with E entire (exp_eq_expRemainder), giving the explicit removable quotient P(h) - 1 = h² Q(h; X,Y,a,b) with Q a polynomial in h, X, Y, a, b and the E(h v_i) (product_sub_one_eq), equal to the dslope quotient of the previous partial for every h (quotient_eq_quotientPoly); Φ = Q · L(h² Q) is then jointly analytic on the open set ‖h² Q‖ < 1 ⊇ {0} × 𝔄⁴, and the bound (iv) follows by continuity of iteratedFDeriv on a compact tube [-h₀, h₀] × K (generalized tube lemma). Not restated separately: the one-variable h-derivatives are directional derivatives of the joint Fréchet derivatives, so they are covered by (iv).

lem:native-scaling.title: Differential-order scaling
lem:native-scaling.note: Proved. The four densities of eq:native-densities are defined concretely (NativeDensity.gravityDensity/ymDensity/higgsDensity/diracDensity, nativeDensity, localAction = h^4 sum) on the periodic grid from the link data of NativeScalingBlocksExact: v(e)=sqrt(-det g), g^{mu nu}=(e^T eta e)^{-1}, e_a^mu e^{b nu}=(e^{-1})^mu_a (e^{-1} eta)^nu_b, gamma^mu(e)=(e^{-1})^mu_a gamma^a, the Cartan plaquette logarithm R^h (series log of lem:native-plaquette, computed in the operator algebra of R^4 via the algebra map Mat -> Op), the gauge field strength F^h, the Higgs link K^h, the Dirac differences with spin link V=e^{h sigma(omega)} rho_S(U) and its explicit inverse V^{-1}=rho_S(U^{-1})e^{-h sigma(omega)} (certified by spinLink_mul_spinLinkInv), potential lambda_H(|H|^2-v_H^2)^2, Yukawa mass term. Main theorem nativeDensity_eq_scaled: for all h,K != 0 and every record, L_h(y)(x) = K^2 normB(hK, K^{-1}, Xi) + K normD(hK, K^{-1}, Xi) exactly, where Xi is the shifted first jet (ShiftedJetAction.stencil over the shifts 0,+-e_mu) of the record together with that of the normalised coframe connection omega~_rho = Omega(e, delta^+_rho e); the cosmological, potential and mass coefficients carry nu^2, nu^2, nu. Summed form localAction_eq_scaled, function identity localAction_eq_scaled_fun, and the Euler-row clause fderiv_localAction_eq_scaled (fderiv S_h = K^2 fderiv A~^B + K fderiv A~^D, given differentiability of the normalised actions). Regularity clause: contDiffAt_normB / contDiffAt_normD (C^infty in (rho,nu,jet) at every point with rho=0, any nu, det e != 0 at the base node) and exists_uniform_bound_normB / exists_uniform_bound_normD (for every order k and compact set of jets in the nondegenerate chart there are rho_0>0, C with all k-th Frechet derivatives bounded by C for |rho|<=rho_0, 0<=nu<=1). Renderings disclosed: (1) the normalised bosonic density is written as a function of the shifted first jets of the record and of omega~_rho (as in the paper's proof 'omega_h = K omega~_rho'), not of second differences of e; the Dirac density depends on the record's jet only; (2) representation data are abstract: rho_H, rho_S continuous algebra homomorphisms, sigma continuous linear, gamma^a arbitrary operators, invariant/Hermitian forms continuous bilinear, Yukawa map continuous linear in H; Higgs and spinor spaces real Banach spaces (Nontrivial), co-spinors are complex-valued functionals, complex structure otherwise unused; (3) plaquettes defined for mu<nu are extended antisymmetrically; (4) 'uniformly regular' rendered as C^infty with uniform derivative bounds on compacts (the growth hypothesis eq:growing-derivatives is not needed for the exact identity); (5) A a real Banach algebra with ||1||=1.

lem:nodal-source-transfer.title: From nodal Euler bounds to a physical source norm
lem:nodal-source-transfer.note: Proved. First clause (NodalSourceTransferExact.lean): ||f||_{L2(Q)} <= sqrt2 ||S_h f||_{0,h;Q'} + sqrt2 |Q'|^{1/2} h L for f with derivative bounded by L on Q', cells meeting Q contained in Q' (the buffer condition provided by Q compactly inside Q' and small h). The O(hK^3) clause is now DERIVED (NodalSourceJetChainExact.lean), not assumed: as in the paper's proof (differential degree <= 2), the Euler density is E_0 = F o j^2 y with j^2 y = (y, Dy, D^2 y) (jet2) and F C^1 on an open set containing a compact jet chart in which the jet of y stays on Q'; y is C^3 near Q' and satisfies eq:growing-derivatives literally on coordinate partial derivatives, ||D^n y(x)(e_{a1}, ..., e_{an})|| <= C K^n for 1 <= n <= 3 (only |alpha| <= 3 of the paper's |alpha| <= q, q >= 5 is used). Partial-derivative bounds give ||D^n y|| <= d^n C K^n (norm_le_card_pow_mul_of_basis), the chain rule gives ||D(j^2 y)|| <= d^3 C K^3 for K >= 1 (norm_jet2Deriv_le_growing), and compactness gives M >= 0 depending only on F and the chart with ||D E_0|| <= M d^3 C K^3 (euler_density_derivative_bound); hence ||E_0||_{L2(Q)} <= sqrt2 ||S_h E_0||_{0,h;Q'} + sqrt2 |Q'|^{1/2} (M d^3 C) h K^3 (eLpNorm_euler_density_le_nodalNorm). Disclosed: F is a general C^1 function of the 2-jet (the concrete Einstein-SM densities are instances); the final 'bounded invertible algebraic change to physical rows' (a fixed bounded linear map) is not formalised; sup norm on R^d. Checklist (l): the derivative bound is no longer a hypothesis; (h): F only C^1 near a compact chart.

lem:native-tail-transfer.title: Finite-order tail bounds
lem:native-tail-transfer.note: e37: ALL CLAUSES PROVED (Sigma = T^3, time periodic box; period-2pi rendering of the record reconstruction, n odd, h = 2pi/n). Setting: z_h = I_h^trig u_h = TrigInterp.recon n u (real trigonometric polynomial over the represented box |l|_inf <= (n-1)/2 with the DFT coefficients; it interpolates the record: recon_gpos), z_h^lo = reconLow n K u (frequencies |l|_inf <= K), tau_{h,j}(K) = sum over the deleted frequencies of (1+|l|_1/K)^j(|a_l|+|b_l|) (TrigInterp.tau; |u_hat| rendered as |a|+|b|). (1) eq:native-tail-derivatives: ||D^i(z_h - z_h^lo)(x)|| <= K^i tau_{h,j}(K) for all i <= j (TrigInterp.norm_iteratedFDeriv_tail_le; full Frechet derivative norm dominates every |d^alpha|, C_j = 1 in the 2pi normalisation; the earlier unit-torus version TrigTail.normalized_deriv_tail_le has C_j = (2pi)^j). Chart sentence: ||z_h - z_h^lo||_inf <= tau_{h,0} <= tau_{h,m} (norm_recon_sub_reconLow_le, tau_mono), and with Bernstein for the low head ||D^j z^lo|| <= (240K)^j A (norm_iteratedFDeriv_reconLow_le, from the scalar Bernstein inequality TrigBernstein.norm_trigDeriv_le |q'| <= 60 K M and VecTrig.norm_iteratedFDeriv_tp_le_bernstein); native_consistency then gives det > 0 and the log chart of the samples of both fields for hK <= c_res (used inside native_euler_tail). (2) eq:native-Euler-tail (NativeTail.native_euler_tail): for a compact coframe chart K_e (det > 0) and amplitude A there are C, c_res, tau_* > 0 such that for every odd n, record u_h, K >= 1 with hK <= c_res, tau_{h,3}(K) <= tau_* (implied by tau_{h,m} small, m = k+2 >= 3), coframes of z^lo and z in K_e and |z^lo| <= A: at EVERY node ||E_h^raw(u_h)(x) - E_h^raw(S_h z^lo)(x)|| <= C K^2 tau_{h,2} (E_h^raw = eulerRow of the unchanged local action NativeDensity.localAction, operator norm on the field fibre), hence the mass norm h^4 sum_x ||.||^2 <= ((2pi)^2 C K^2 tau_{h,2})^2 over the whole periodic box (so on every Q'). Proof as in the paper: u_h = S_h z_h (recon_gpos); lem:native-scaling on raw rows gives the factor K^2 (eulerRow_local_eq_scaled); the normalised rows of the K-rescaled fields differ by the mean-value bound EulerRowDiff.norm_eulerRow_sub_le (shifted jets through second order, uniform C^3 density bounds on a compact jet set). (3) eq:native-source-tail (NativeTail.native_source_tail): R_B, R_D are DEFINED as the bosonic / Dirac components of the continuum Euler covector E_0(z) = contEuler of the limit density L_0 = limDensity(firstJetDensity D) applied to the reconstruction (RB, RD; Dirac rows first order: eulerOp_comp_ιS, Ddens_decomp); sobX k Q f = (sum_{i<=k} int_Q ||D_x^i f||^2)^{1/2} with spatial iterated derivatives (L^2_t H^k_x on any measurable Q inside the periodic box). For every k there are C, tau_* with: tau_{h,k+2} <= tau_*, low coframe in K_e, |z^lo| <= A imply sobX k (R_B(z)-R_B(z^lo)) + sobX (k+1) (R_D(z)-R_D(z^lo)) <= C K^{k+2} tau_{h,k+2}; Faa di Bruno difference bounds CompDiff.norm_iteratedFDeriv_comp_sub_le and ContEulerBounds.norm_iteratedFDeriv_eulerOp_sub_le / foOp_sub_le (every term carries a tail factor, at most k+2 field derivatives) plus contEuler_native_scale (K^2 bosonic, K Dirac). (4) zero-order physical source difference: second clause of native_source_tail, ||R_B(z)-R_B(z^lo)||_{L^2(Q)} + ||R_D(z)-R_D(z^lo)||_{L^2(Q)} <= C K^2 tau_{h,2}. Non-vacuity: native_tail_hyps_const (constant records with coframe in K_e have tau = 0 and constant full/low heads, via residue orthogonality sum_cexp_phase_zmod; every odd n, K >= 0). Renderings disclosed: 2pi-periodic box; |u_hat| = |a|+|b|; sup norms via Frechet operator norms; the constants depend on (K_e, A, k) only; 'smooth algebraic dependence of metric/frame' is not a separate statement (the rows are composed with the field heads directly). Standard axioms only.

lem:log-source-upgrade.title: Logarithmic derivative upgrade for a band-limited source
lem:log-source-upgrade.note: Proved. Complex-analytic step (StripHolomorphicFourierDecay.lean): a function holomorphic on the strip |Im z| < b, 1-periodic on R and bounded by A there has |int_0^1 e^{-2pi i n x} g(x) dx| <= A e^{-2 pi b |n|} (periodicity propagates to the strip by the identity theorem, periodic_on_strip; contour shift by Cauchy on the rectangle [0,1] x [0,y], vertical sides cancel, integral_eq_integral_shift; shift by -+ i b', b' -> b). On the torus T^d: if every coordinate restriction s -> F(x + s e_i) through every real point extends holomorphically to the strip with bound A then |F_hat(n)| <= A e^{-2 pi b |n_i|} for all i (Haar translation invariance + Fubini reduce to the line estimate), hence <= A e^{-2 pi b |n|_inf} (norm_mFourierCoeff_le_of_strip). The rectangle contour was used instead of the annulus/Laurent route (equivalent, and it is the paper's 'contour shifting'). Upgrade (AnalyticSourceSobolevUpgrade.lean): lattice tail sum sum_n <n>^{2j} e^{-gamma|n|_inf} <= M_{j,d} gamma^{-(2j+d)}; frequency split ||c||^2_{H^j} <= (1+4pi^2 d B^2)^j ||c||^2_{l2} + A^2 e^{-gamma B} M gamma^{-(2j+d)}; its L^2_t H^j_x version over any measure space of times; Parseval for continuous slices; and log_source_upgrade: for fixed a > 0, integer j and finite time measure mu there is C = C_{j,d,a,mu(I)} > 0 such that for all continuous slices f(t) on T^d extending holomorphically along coordinate lines to width a/K (period-2pi units; a/(2 pi K) on the unit torus) with bound A >= 0, K >= 1, and int_I int_T |f|^2 <= eps^2 (eps > 0): every slice is in H^j and ||f||^2_{L^2_t H^j_x} <= (C eps K^j [1 + log(2 + C A K^{j+d}/eps)]^j)^2 (d = 3 gives K^{j+3}); the frequency threshold is B = 2K Lambda/min(a,1) as in the paper. eps = 0: log_source_upgrade_zero (the L^2_t H^j_x norm vanishes). Renderings: unit torus (constants absorb the 2pi dilation), Fourier H^j norm with weight (1+4pi^2|n|^2)^j, complex scalar sources (vector rows componentwise), holomorphy required only along coordinate lines (weaker than the paper's extension in the three spatial variables), hypothesis eps <= 1 not needed. Non-vacuity: Fourier monomials satisfy the strip hypothesis (strip_extension_mFourier) and the constant source satisfies all hypotheses (example in the file).

prop:native-rounding.title: A sufficient nodal-accuracy condition
prop:native-rounding.note: Proved on the periodic grid (Fin 4 -> ZMod n) with the normalized four-dimensional DFT u^(l) = n^{-4} sum_x e(-l.x) u(x) defined from the product of Mathlib's standard characters ZMod.stdAddChar: character orthogonality sum_l e(l.x) = n^4 [x = 0] (sum_char4) and Parseval sum_l ||u^(l)||^2 = n^{-4} sum_x ||u(x)||^2 (sum_norm_dft4_sq). Modes are measured by centred representatives ZMod.valMinAbs (|l|_1 = sum_mu |l_mu|, tail set |l|_inf > K), so Lambda_h is the mode lattice and tau_{h,j}(K) of eq:native-tail is the definition tau. eq:native-rounding-tail: if u = u^b + e with u^b Fourier-supported in |l|_inf <= K and max_x ||e(x)|| <= eps, then with h = 2 pi / n and hK <= 1, tau_{h,j}(K) <= (1 + 4 pi)^j 4 pi^2 eps h^{-2} (hK)^{-j} (tau_le_of_bandLimited_add; explicit C_j). eq:native-rounding-tolerance: eps <= c h^{m+3} K^{m+2} gives tau_{h,m} <= C_m c hK^2 (tau_le_of_tolerance) and, with m = k + 2, tau_{h,2} <= C_2 c (h^k K^{k+1}) hK, so tau_{h,2} = O(hK) as soon as h^k K^{k+1} is bounded, which holds on the rate families K ~ h^{-beta}, beta < 1/(k+4), of cor:native-rate (tau_two_le_of_tolerance, with the family entering through the explicit hypothesis h^k K^{k+1} <= A). Scoped hypotheses (disclosed): hK <= 1 (the paper's standing hK <= c_res), K real positive, the record valued in a complex inner-product space E (real-valued records embed in C^d), n is any nonzero integer (oddness is not needed), and the 'affine field-chart constraints' clause plays no role in the inequality.

cor:native-rate.title: An explicit cofinal rate
cor:native-rate.note: Self-contained asymptotics PROVED (DyadicRateAsymptotics.lean), along any filter: with the budget of eq:native-forcing-budget encoded literally (eps0, epsc, logFactor, forcingBudget, any C_k >= 0) and the hypotheses sigma_h = O(h), 1 <= K_h <= c2 h^{-beta}, tau_{h,2} = O(hK), tau_{h,k+2} = O(hK^2) (eq:native-tail-rate), 0 < h <= 1: h K^3 <= eps_{c,h} <= C h K^3 (le_epsc, epsc_le), L_{h,k} <= C_L(1+|log h|) (logFactor_le), F_{h,k} = O(h^{1-beta(k+4)}(1+|log h|)^{k+1}) (forcingBudget_isBigO, explicit constant in forcingBudget_le), eps_{0,h} = O(h^{1-3beta}) (eps0_isBigO) and its transfer to eps^phys under the zero-order estimate eps^phys <= C eps_{0,h} (physical_isBigO_of_le; that estimate is eq:native-zero-source of the open thm:native-source), F_{h,k} -> 0 when beta < 1/(k+4) (forcingBudget_tendsto_zero, with a non-vacuity example h = 1/(n+1), K = h^{-1/18}), dyadic summability sum_n h_n^rho (1+|log h_n|)^p < oo for h_n = h_0 2^{-n} (summable_dyadic) and summability of adjacent differences from bounds against a common reference (summable_adjacent_of_le), and the worked exponents 5/9, 5/6 for k = 4, beta = 1/18 (native_rate_example_exponents). Only the upper bound K <= c2 h^{-beta} of K ~ h^{-beta} is needed. NOT PROVED: the state/curvature/stress convergence rates, which apply thm:native-closure (open) and thm:native-source (open); strict corollary policy keeps the record conditional.

prop:initial-constraint-retraction.title: Uniform initial-constraint retraction
prop:initial-constraint-retraction.note: Proved on the structure ExactInitialConstraintReduction (def:exact-initial-reduction). initialConstraintRetraction_derivAtZero is the literal statement: with A_h := D_λΦ_h(0) (fderivWithin on the closed ball |λ| ≤ r_*, where Φ_h is C¹), σ_min(A_h) ≥ γ_* rendered as γ_*‖v‖ ≤ ‖A_h v‖ ∀v (the definition of the smallest singular value in the Euclidean norm), the margin ‖DΦ_h(λ) − A_h‖ ≤ γ_*/2 on |λ| ≤ r_*, |Φ_h(0)| ≤ β_h and 2γ_*⁻¹β_h ≤ r_*: there is a unique zero λ_h of Φ_h in the closed ball of radius 2γ_*⁻¹β_h, and every such zero gives d_h = ι_h(λ_h) with 𝔠_k(d_h) = 0 (exact factorization, not the contraction) and ‖d_h − 𝒰(ẑ_h)(0)‖ ≤ 2B_*γ_*⁻¹β_h. initialConstraintRetraction is the same for an arbitrary linear A with these margins. Proof as in the paper: invertibility of A from the lower bound (finite dimension), mean-value inequality for N = Φ − A, the frozen-inverse map T = λ − A⁻¹Φ is a 1/2-contraction of the ball into itself, Banach fixed point (ContractingWith) on the complete closed ball. Scoped hypothesis disclosed: 0 ≤ B_* (implicit for a Lipschitz constant). The closing remarks (only the initial datum is corrected; tube membership separate) are commentary, not formalized.

cor:validated-initial-retraction.title: Validated constraint evaluation with an explicit error budget
cor:validated-initial-retraction.note: Proved by instantiating the (proved) parent prop:initial-constraint-retraction (initialConstraintRetraction) with the frozen matrix A~_h = D Phi~_h(0) applied to the exact retained map R.retained: the two derivative margins of eq:validated-initial-margins give ||D Phi_h - A~_h|| <= gamma_*/2 on the correction ball by the triangle inequality, and |Phi_h(0)| <= |Phi~_h(0)| + zeta_0 = beta^eff. Conclusion: unique zero of the exact reduced map in the closed ball of radius 2 gamma_*^{-1} beta^eff, corrected datum in the exact constraint set, displacement <= 2 B_* gamma_*^{-1} beta^eff. Renderings: sigma_min(A~) >= gamma_* as gamma_* ||v|| <= ||A~ v|| for all v (Euclidean definition of the least singular value); derivatives are fderivWithin on the closed correction ball |lambda| <= r_* where the maps are C^1; scoped hypothesis 0 <= B_* (Lipschitz constant). The 'in every shadow estimate beta_h is replaced by beta^eff' sentence is the bookkeeping consequence of the same conclusion.

prop:shadow-residual-upgrade.title: Full-record residual interpolation
prop:shadow-residual-upgrade.note: Proved (generic, Analysis/TorusSobolevEmbedding.lean, earlier): the interpolation inequality ||u||_{H^k} <= ||u||_{L^2}^{1-k/s} ||u||_{H^s}^{k/s} on T^d (periodic space-time box for d = 4) and its L^2_t H^k_x form lintegral_sobSq_interpolation. Not proved: (i) eq:shadow-zero-residual, which the proof takes from prop:native-consistency (open; strict corollary policy) with lem:nodal-source-transfer (proved); (ii) the cutoff-independent H^s bound of the differentiated bosonic/Dirac Euler rows from the reader reserve eq:shadow-reader-reserve (nonlinear Moser/product estimates for the continuum rows, which are not defined in Lean as functions of the field); (iii) interpolation in the full space-time H^k(Q) norm (time derivatives included) on the non-periodic cylinder Q = I x T^3 (needs an extension operator in t).

lem:half-ricci.title: Twisted half-Ricci contraction
lem:half-ricci.note: Proved as a pointwise algebraic identity: for a Clifford frame (c_a in any associative real algebra, ε_a = ±1, c_ac_b + c_bc_a = -2ε_aδ_ab, any finite index type) and any array R_abcd antisymmetric in both pairs with the first Bianchi identity, Σ_b ε_b c_b R^∇_ba = ½Σ_b ε_b (Σ_c ε_c R_cabc) c_b + Σ_b ε_b c_b ρ(F_ba), where R^∇ = ¼Σ ε_cε_d R_abcd c_c c_d + ρ(F) (twisted_half_ricci_contraction; half_ricci_contraction; with the contraction Σ_c ε_c R_cacb the sign of the Ricci term flips, half_ricci_contraction_opposite). Convention matching: the paper's Ric_ab = R^c_{acb} = Σ_c ε_c Riem_cacb, and the true spin curvature for this Clifford sign is -¼Σ Riem_abcd c^c c^d; instantiating R := -Riem gives eq:half-ricci verbatim for the geometric twisted curvature with the paper's Ricci convention (the displayed R^S formula of the manuscript must be read with R_abcd = -Riem_abcd, or carry -¼). The identification of R with the torsion-free spin-connection curvature and of ρ(F) with the gauge curvature is the lemma's setting, not part of the algebraic claim.

prop:spinor-prolongation.title: Residual-sensitive tangential spinor prolongation
prop:spinor-prolongation.note: PROVED as exact algebra on jets at a point in an orthonormal moving frame (the rendering already accepted for lem:half-ricci and lem:harmonic-defect-forcing), any finite frame index type. Setting (LCJet): lowered Levi-Civita coefficients G_abc = <nabla_{e_a} e_b, e_c> (antisymmetric in b,c) with frame-derivative jets, torsion-free structure functions Lambda = Gamma - Gamma^T, the Jacobi identity of the frame (hypothesis on jets; satisfied by every smooth frame), gauge potential rho_a commuting with Clifford multiplication; the twisted spin connection omega_a = 1/4 sum eps_c eps_d G_acd c_c c_d + rho_a. PROVED (not assumed): Clifford multiplication is parallel (clifford_parallel, via comm_spinPart), so(eta)->A is a Lie map (bracket_spinPart), the twisted curvature is R^nabla_ab = 1/4 sum eps eps Rm_abxy c_x c_y + rho(F_ab) with Rm_abxy = <R(e_a,e_b)e_x,e_y> of the frame connection and F the gauge curvature (curv_eq), Rm has both antisymmetries, the first Bianchi identity (from Jacobi + torsion-freeness), pair symmetry and the half-Ricci Bianchi form. eq:spinor-prolongation VERBATIM: LCJet.spinor_prolongation: (D^{T*}X)_a = Sum_b eps_b c_b nabla^2_{ba}Psi = M X_a + M_H[D_aH]Psi + nabla_a r_D + 1/2 Ric_ab c^b Psi + c^b rho(F_ba) Psi, c^b = eps_b c_b, Ric_ab = sum_c eps_c Rm_cabc = the standard Ricci tensor tr(Z -> R(Z,e_a)e_b) (this fixes the sign question noted under lem:half-ricci: no sign flip is needed when R^S is computed from the actual spin connection). Proof as in the paper: commute nabla_a with the twisted Dirac operator (dTX_eq: Ricci identity ricci_identity + covDirac_eq), covariant product rule for the affine mass map M(H) = m0 + M_H[H] (covDirac_eq_mass; hypotheses: M(w) commutes with the spin rotations c_c c_d and [rho_a, M(w)] = M_H[rho_H(A_a)w], i.e. gauge-equivariant Yukawa/mass map), then lem:half-ricci (twisted_half_ricci_contraction). eq:normal-spinor-jet: normal_spinor_jet / normal_spinor_jet_resD (Lorentzian frame eps_0 = -1, eps_i = 1): X_0 = c_0 sum_i c_i X_i - c_0 M Psi - c_0 r_D. 'no time derivative of r_D': nabla_a r_D = e_a r_D + omega_a r_D involves only r_D and its derivative along e_a (covR_local), and in the prolonged rows the residual enters only through nabla_a r_D (ActualJetWriter.lc_prolonged_row); X_0 enters algebraically. Disclosed rendering: identities on jets (frame-commutator relation on the spinor 2-jet, Jacobi identity of the frame, constancy of the c_a in the frame trivialisation are the jet conventions satisfied by smooth fields). Non-vacuity: lorentz2 (real 2x2 Lorentzian Clifford frame), flatLC.

lem:harmonic-defect-forcing.title: Exact harmonic-defect forcing identity
lem:harmonic-defect-forcing.note: Proved as an exact pointwise identity on the metric 2-jet (the jet convention of Gravity/CoordinateCurvature.lean), over any finite index type with Fintype.card n = 4 where traces enter. Data at a point: g, its inverse gi (g gi = 1, gi symmetric), dg = dg_{mu nu}/dx^alpha, ddg (symmetric in the two derivative and in the two metric indices); the derived jets are those of the product rule: d(g^{-1}) = -g^{-1} dg g^{-1} (dginv, and dginv_unique shows it is forced by differentiating g g^{-1} = 1), Gamma = chr, dGamma = dchr1 + dchr2, C^mu = g^{ab}Gamma^mu_{ab}, nabla_mu C_nu = d_mu(g_{nu l} C^l) - Gamma^l_{mu nu} C_l, nabla_a C^a := g^{ab} nabla_a C_b (metric compatibility). Results: reducedEinstein_eq (hat G = G - H, eq:reduced-Einstein/eq:harmonic-defect-tensor), trG_defectTensor (tr_g H = -nabla_a C^a in 4D), harmonic_residual_trace_reversal (eq:harmonic-residual-trace-reversal, any T, Lambda, kappa), ricci_sub_symDefect (Ric - nabla_(mu C_nu) = -1/2 g^{ab} d_a d_b g_{mu nu} + Q_{mu nu} with the explicit remainder qRem(g, g^{-1}, dg) containing no second derivatives; principal-part cancellation in principal_part), qRem_smul (Q quadratic: Q(t dg) = t^2 Q(dg)), qRem_contDiff (Q is C^infinity, polynomial in (g, g^{-1}, dg)), ricci_trace_reversal (eq:trace-reversal-residual), off_harmonic_metric_wave (eq:off-harmonic-metric-wave). Rendering disclosed: the identity is stated on 2-jets at a point (which is what 'every smooth field tuple satisfies' means pointwise); the passage from a smooth metric field to its jets (that the jet formulas are the actual derivatives) is the product rule and is not re-derived with fderiv, except for the inverse-metric jet (dginv_unique).

prop:actual-jet-writer.title: Gauge-defect-aware block-symmetric actual-jet equation
prop:actual-jet-writer.note: Clause-level (jets at a point on the adapted frame e_0 = N^-1(d_t - beta^j d_j), e_a = e_a^j d_j, coordinates Fin 4). PROVED: (i) metric rows of the first-order wave reduction: head row d_t u = N p + beta^j d_j u with d_j u algebraic in q (head_row, spatial_of_q); p-row d_t p - beta^j d_j p - N e_a^j d_j q_a = N(-g^{ab}d_a d_b u + L_p) for any frame adapted to g^{-1} (p_row); q-row (q_row, Schwarz); for u = g_{mu nu}, with lem:harmonic-defect-forcing, metric_p_row: the p-row equals N(L_p - 2Q + 2kappa(T - 1/2 g trT) + 2Lambda g) + 2N E^tr + G with the gauge forcing G = -2N nabla_(mu C_nu); eq:actual-jet-gauge-forcing exactly (gaugeForce_eq): G = J_C C + J_C^0 d_t C + sum_j J_C^j d_j C with dC the actual derivative jet of the harmonic defect, J_C^mu = -N(delta g + delta g) depending only on (N,g) (Jd, Jd_depends), J_C on (N,g,dg) (JC); no second derivative of C; C = 0, dC = 0 => G = 0 (gaugeForce_zero); the wave-block principal matrices are symmetric (waveSym_symm, p_row_symbol). lem:actual-jet-complete-forcing.title: Derivative-counted complete forcing bound
lem:actual-jet-complete-forcing.note: Analytic core PROVED on the slices of [0,T] x T^d (classical squared H^k norms Q_k of SlabSobolevAlgebra; k >= 2m-1 with m > d/2, i.e. k >= 3 on T^3, covering k >= 4): for every forcing of the displayed form of eq:actual-jet-writer, F_err = sum b_i R_B,i + sum q_{kappa j} d_j R_D,kappa + sum_l (c_l C^l + c0_l d_t C^l + sum_j cj_l d_j C^l) with smooth periodic zeroth-order coefficients bounded in H^k by M: Q_k(F_err) <= 8 C_alg M (|iota| + |kappa| d^2 + |theta|(2+d^2)) (sum Q_k(R_B) + sum Q_{k+1}(R_D) + sum Q_{k+1}(C) + sum Q_k(d_t C)) (forcing_bound; H^k algebra Q_mul_le, derivative counting Q_pd_le: the differentiated Dirac residual and harmonic defect cost one extra derivative, d_t C none), and the norm form of eq:actual-jet-complete-forcing (forcing_bound_norm). The coefficient hypothesis holds for coefficient maps polynomial in the state fields on an H^k ball (coeff_bound_poly, Moser for polynomials via evalF_lip), which covers the gauge-forcing coefficients J_C^mu, J_C of gaugeForce_eq. Not closed: the form of F_err is the conclusion of the open prop:actual-jet-writer (corollary policy), and smooth (non-polynomial) coefficient maps (lapse (-g^00)^-1/2, frame square roots, inverse metric) need a general Moser composition estimate (only polynomials and matrix inverses exist). e37: not advanced in this batch (the batch effort went into lem:native-tail-transfer); status unchanged.

prop:coupled-bootstrap.title: Coupled actual-jet stability and first-exit closure
prop:coupled-bootstrap.note: Linear estimate and bootstrap skeleton PROVED (generic, T^d slab, first-order systems d_t W + A^j d_j W with Hermitian W^{1,inf} coefficients, A^0 = 1; real symmetric realified systems are a special case): hk_energy_estimate: if every d^alpha W, |alpha| <= k, satisfies SymHyp on [0,T] and the commuted forcing satisfies sum_alpha ||sum_mu A^mu d_mu d^alpha W||^2_{L2} <= K1 E_k + Phi, then E_k(t) <= e^{KT}(|N|^2 Cb E_k(0) + |N| int_0^T Phi) exp(e^{KT}|N| K1 t) (eq:actual-jet-gauge-energy integrated, eq:actual-jet-integrated-stability; per-word L2 estimate l2_energy_estimate + integral Gronwall integral_gronwall). first_exit_bootstrap: if on every initial interval inside the tube E_k <= rho the coefficient hypotheses hold with uniform constants and the commuted-forcing bound holds, and the initial state is in the smaller tube with bound < rho, then E_k <= bound on all of [0,T]; continuity of E_k (existence of the smooth record on the slab) is the only global input, no all-time H^k bound is assumed. thm:hyperbolic.title: Common-slab metric stability
thm:hyperbolic.note: PROVED (rendering disclosed). Sigma = T^3; fields smooth and Z^3-periodic on R^{1+3}, hypotheses on the slab [0,T] x R^3, T > 0, s >= 5. Hypotheses = the paper's, MetricHypSh (ReducedWaveShiftData.lean): symmetric metric g with inverse field gi (g gi = 1 on the slab); uniform hyperbolicity with the common time function t = x^0 encoded literally as dt uniformly timelike (g^{00} <= -a0) and uniformly spacelike slices (g_{ij} xi^i xi^j >= lamS |xi|^2); the uniform inverse-metric bound |g^{ab}| <= Lambda; eq:hyperbolic-bound as classical squared slice norms Q_s(g_c)(t), Q_{s-1}(d_t g_c)(t) <= K0; eq:reduced-wave g^{ab} d_a d_b g_c = N_c(g, dg) + S_c with N a polynomial in (g^{-1}, g, dg, fixed smooth periodic background fields) (the reduced Einstein(-matter) operator form, disclosed as in the earlier passes). NO sign condition on g^{ij}: any bounded shift is allowed (shifted_metricHypSh: a constant metric with shift 2, so d_t is spacelike and g^{11} = -3; shifted_not_metricHyp: the earlier rendering MetricHyp with positive g^{ij} fails for it). G2 (paper: proof of thm:hyperbolic, 'use the differentiated normal derivative as energy multiplier ... The uniformly spacelike slices and bounded lapse and shift give a positive wave energy': a nonzero shift is allowed, so option (a)): SlabWaveShiftEnergy.lean builds the normal-derivative-multiplier energy E_S = int sum_b ((d_t u - beta^k d_k u)^2 + a^{ij} d_i u d_j u + u^2), a = gamma + beta beta (= N^2 h^{-1}): pointwise identity d_t e - div J = G free of second derivatives (shift_alg), G <= K |first jets|^2, sqrt_energyS_le (L^1_t L^2_x source, Gronwall), sqrt_energyS_le_of_forcing, the H^k version hkS_energy / hkS_energy_of_forcing via the existing prolongation (SysHyp with an arbitrary gamma-coercivity constant + coercivity of a + |d_t beta| bound), energySK_ge, energySK_le_size, energySK_tendsto_zero. MetricHypSh.coer_acoef: a(xi,xi) >= lamS/(9 Lambda (C_S K0 + 1)) |xi|^2 (shift_coer_alg: with V = g^{-1}(-q p, xi), V^0 = 0, xi_i = g_{ij} V^j, a(xi,xi) = -q g_{ij} V^i V^j); abs_pd_beta_time. The reduced chain under MetricHypSh: diffSys_hyp_any, forcing_Q_le_sh, EdiffS_equiv (difference energy uniformly equivalent to ||g_h - g_j||^2_{H^{s-1}} + ||d_t g_h - d_t g_j||^2_{H^{s-2}}), hyperbolic_energy_sh (eq:hyperbolic-energy with a_{h,j} = (16 + ||S_j||^2_{H^{s-2}})^{1/2}, sup int a < infinity by sources_bounded), common_slab_cauchy_sh; common_slab_limit_sh and common_slab_limit_weak_sh (first two limits: g_h -> g in C_t H^{s-1}, d_t g_h -> d_t g in C_t H^{s-2}, the time derivative by FTC, and the C_t H^m limit components are the weak spatial derivatives of g(t), d_t g(t) on T^3, weak_deriv_of_L2_limit); coframe_convergence_sh (coframe clause, eq:strong-geometry); riem_cauchy_sh (CtxS: the uniform Lipschitz calculus of ReducedWaveSlabLipschitz/Curvature restated without a sign of the gamma-coercivity constant). G1: riem_limit_sh: g_h -> g, d g_h -> dg, g_h^{-1} -> g^{-1} uniformly on the slab; g is differentiable on the open slab with partial derivatives dg (hasFDerivAt_of_UConv) and g g^{-1} = 1; for every curvature component q and word |w| <= s-3, d^w Riem(g_h) converges in L^1((0,T); L^2([0,1]^3)) to an integrable curve R_{q,w} (exists_L1_limit); R_{q,wi} = d_i R_{q,w} weakly on (0,T) x T^3 (so R_q in L^1_t H^{s-3}); and R_q = Riem(g)_q as distributions on (0,T) x T^3 tested on IsCylTest functions (smooth, spatially periodic, compact time support; exists_cylTest), Riem(g) := riemDist T (GamL g^{-1} dg), the distributional Riemann tensor int int (-Gamma^a_{db} d_c phi + Gamma^a_{cb} d_d phi + (Gamma Gamma - Gamma Gamma) phi) of the C^1 metric g (slabInt_riemF identifies it with the classical pairing for smooth metrics by integration by parts on the cylinder, slabInt_pd_mul; tendsto_riemDist passes to the limit). Since d_t^2 g exists only in L^1_t H^{s-3}, the distributional curvature of the C^1 limit metric is the meaning of Riem(g). Vanishing reduced-equation residual: covered (S_h is any smooth source). Non-vacuity examples with the shifted metric for common_slab_cauchy_sh, common_slab_limit_sh, riem_limit_sh, common_slab_limit_weak_sh. Standard axioms only, no sorry.

prop:subsidiary.title: Subsidiary equation and constraint stability
prop:subsidiary.note: PROVED (Sigma = T^3 disclosed). eq:subsidiary: SourcedHyp.subsidiary — for a classical metric field g = eta + Q on [0,T] x T^3 (C3Field with derivative fields up to order 3; regularity as in C3Field.Hyp, nondegenerate g) and stress/residual tensor fields Ts, r with first-derivative fields, satisfying the reduced Einstein equation G_hat + Lambda g = kappa Ts + r (eq:reduced-Einstein, the library's resM) on the slab with constants Lambda, kappa, the harmonic gauge covector C = C(g) satisfies Box C_nu + Ric_nu^mu C_mu = -2 W_nu, W = kappa div Ts + div r, at every interior point: the reduced equation is differentiated along consistent time/space jet paths (Jet3.PathDeriv.resM + uniqueness of derivatives) and fed to SubsidiarySource.subsidiary_with_source (contracted Bianchi + commutation identity). eq:constraint-bound: constraint_bound — under WaveCoeffs (uniform wave-energy coefficients: -g^00 >= a0 > 0, g^ij xi xi >= lambda|xi|^2, |d g^{-1}| <= M; the lower-order part of the subsidiary operator — Christoffel and curvature potential — has operator norm <= m(t), m >= 0 continuous, i.e. an L^1_t L^inf_x potential) and -g^00(0) <= A1, |g^ij(0)| <= A1: for every t in [0,T], ||(C, dC)(t)||_{L^2} <= C_T (||(C, dC)(0)||_{L^2} + int_0^T ||W||_{L^2}), with the explicit C_T = constC = 2 c^{-1/2} max(sqrt(3A1+1), c^{-1/2}) exp(((16M+2)T + 4 int_0^T m)/(2c)), c = min(a0, lambda, 1). Proof: the subsidiary system is a forced linear wave system (forcedSolves: principal part -g^00 d_t^2 C = 2 g^0i d_i d_t C + g^ij d_i d_j C, potential lowerOp, forcing 2W); the generic forced energy inequality E' <= k(t)E + 2c^{-1/2}||F||_{L^2} sqrt E (ForcedSolves.energy_deriv_le, energy identity by integration by parts on T^3) and the square-root Gronwall with L^1 source (sqrt_energy_gronwall: applied to (E+delta)^{1/2}, delta -> 0, exactly as in the manuscript). The final sentence: constraint_vanishes (zero initial constraint data and zero Ward residual force C = dC = 0 on the slab) and constraint_tendsto (families with common a0, lambda, M, A1 and uniformly bounded int m: initial data + ||W||_{L^1L^2} -> 0 implies sup_t ||(C,dC)||_{L^2} -> 0). Disclosed: m continuous (the L^1 norm enters the constant; smooth fields give continuous sup-norms); the fields are classical C^3 metric fields (the manuscript's smooth reconstructed field). Non-vacuity: flat metric with zero sources (flat_sourced, flat_coeffs, example using constraint_bound); ForcedSolves non-vacuity quadSol_forced (u = t^2/2, W = 1).

prop:generated-initial.note: PROVED (Sigma = T^3, the manuscript's setting for app:generated-dynamics; conditional on ass:constrained-initial-solver as the statement says). prop:native-reader.title: Exact native-energy to physical-tail certificate
prop:native-reader.note: Finite-dimensional linear algebra, fully proved; the revised statement matches the Lean even more closely than the old one. Source space H = finite-dimensional real inner-product space, native energy Q symmetric with <xi,Q xi> >= 0, coefficient map T : H -> (modes -> F) linear, positive weights w, tail tau_w(v) = sum_l w_l ||v_l|| (the l^1(w) norm). eq:source-reader-linear / eq:source-reader-kernel: exists_readerConstant_iff_kernel states that a finite c with ||T xi||_{l^1(w)} <= c <xi,Q xi>^{1/2} for ALL xi in H (IsReaderConstant, quantified over the entire source space, so not inferred from a finite list of legal states) exists iff T(ker Q) = 0 (KernelCondition). eq:source-reader-constant: readerConstant := ||T Q^{dagger/2}||_{2->l^1(w)} = sup_{||y||<=1} tau_w(T Q^{dagger/2} y), with Q^{dagger/2} = SpectralDiag.pinvSqrt built from Mathlib's finite spectral theorem (lambda_i^{-1/2} on the nonzero spectrum, 0 on the kernel); symmetric, positive, and its square satisfies the Penrose identities Q Q^dagger Q = Q and Q^dagger Q Q^dagger = Q^dagger (Q_pinvSq_Q, pinvSq_Q_pinvSq), so it is the positive square root of the Moore-Penrose inverse; readerConstant_isLeast: under the kernel condition this constant is admissible and is the least nonnegative admissible constant. eq:source-reader-tail ("in particular"): affine_reader_tail derives tau_w(u^soft + T xi) <= tau_w(u^soft) + c <xi,Q xi>^{1/2} for the affine reader u = u^soft + R xi by the triangle inequality. Disclosed: T is any linear coefficient map (its identification with the |l|_inf > K weighted Fourier coefficients of R_h xi is carried abstractly); optimality is stated among nonnegative constants.
